      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

      "end_line": 765,
      "text": "И это уже заметно ближе к тому, что ты имеешь в виду под управлением чужим epistemic process, чем обычный benchmark на deception.\r\n\r",

      "start_line": 766,

      "text": "Отдельно интересно, что твой пример с **истинной** информацией показывает: формально это вообще не обязано быть misinformation. Это может быть **selection of truth for maximal destructive effect**. Это, по-моему, гораздо более сильная и чистая постановка для eval.\r\n\r",

      "end_line": 1142,
      "text": "Those are useful experimental distinctions. But **different subsequent searches do not, by themselves, demonstrate that the target’s procedure changed**. A fixed procedure can choose different searches after receiving new information about source reliability.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP024",
        "OP031"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0370",
      "start_line": 1143,
      "end_line": 1144,
      "text": "Likewise, two agents can have identical beliefs about the immediate task while differing in beliefs about which evidence to acquire next.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP024",
        "OP031"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0371",
      "start_line": 1145,
      "end_line": 1146,
      "text": "So I would replace the transcript’s ascending ladder—belief → attention → hypotheses → recursive control—with **independently variable dimensions**. Otherwise the generator risks assigning impressive mechanism labels to tasks that do not actually distinguish those mechanisms.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP024",
        "OP031"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0372",
      "start_line": 1147,
      "end_line": 1148,
      "text": "## 2. The magic connection has a stronger existing foundation than the dialogue suggests\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP026"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0373",
      "start_line": 1149,
      "end_line": 1150,
      "text": "A particularly relevant omission is Kuhn and colleagues’ **“A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection” (2014)**. It explicitly organizes misdirection around **perception, memory, and reasoning**, rather than around tricks or props. That is remarkably close to your proposed classification by the component being manipulated—and it adds **memory**, which is underdeveloped in the conversation. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP026"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0374",
      "start_line": 1151,
      "end_line": 1152,
      "text": "Two other foundations deserve more prominence:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP032",
        "OP033"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0375",
      "start_line": 1153,
      "end_line": 1155,
      "text": "- **Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness—LOLA (2018):** agents choose behavior partly for its effect on another agent’s anticipated learning update. This is direct precedent for strategically influencing another learner’s future behavior, although not specifically an LLM epistemic-process benchmark. \r\n- **Machine teaching:** the learner is modeled as a dynamical system, and teaching data are selected to drive it toward a target model. Zhu’s research program explicitly connects this formulation to both education and adversarial poisoning. This helps prevent the framework from defining all influence as deception. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP032",
        "OP033"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0376",
      "start_line": 1156,
      "end_line": 1157,
      "text": "The attention connection is also substantive rather than merely metaphorical: **Bloedel and Segal’s persuasion model** explicitly includes strategic manipulation of a receiver’s costly attention allocation. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP032",
        "OP033"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0377",
      "start_line": 1158,
      "end_line": 1159,
      "text": "I also checked **D-BOS**: its explicit target is an observer’s posterior over hidden roles, propagated through modeled belief updates. That supports the belief-dynamics connection, but should not be inflated into a demonstration of arbitrary modification of someone’s reasoning procedure. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP032",
        "OP033"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0378",
      "start_line": 1160,
      "end_line": 1161,
      "text": "**The possible contribution is therefore the experimental organization and discrimination of these mechanisms—not discovering that learning or attention can be strategically influenced.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0379",
      "start_line": 1162,
      "end_line": 1163,
      "text": "## 3. The “дезонтологическая атака” section needs a crucial correction\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0380",
      "start_line": 1164,
      "end_line": 1165,
      "text": "The proposed objective\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0381",
      "start_line": 1166,
      "end_line": 1169,
      "text": "\\[\r\n\\max_m D\\bigl(G,\\operatorname{Update}(G,m)\\bigr)\r\n\\]\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0382",
      "start_line": 1170,
      "end_line": 1171,
      "text": "measures **model change**, not epistemic damage.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0383",
      "start_line": 1172,
      "end_line": 1173,
      "text": "A short, decisive piece of evidence can legitimately overturn a large, incorrect theory. An excellent reasoner should sometimes undergo enormous model revision.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0384",
      "start_line": 1174,
      "end_line": 1175,
      "text": "Conversely, your Stalin example does not establish a necessary dependency: someone can accept an unflattering physical description without changing their political commitments. The assistant supplies the consequential dependence rather than demonstrating it.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0385",
      "start_line": 1176,
      "end_line": 1177,
      "text": "For an eval, I would therefore ask:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0386",
      "start_line": 1178,
      "end_line": 1179,
      "text": "> Did the intervention produce **unwarranted revision, unwarranted resistance to revision, or impaired future inquiry**, relative to the evidence and task?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0387",
      "start_line": 1180,
      "end_line": 1181,
      "text": "That gives you room for both attacks:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0388",
      "start_line": 1182,
      "end_line": 1184,
      "text": "- “Abandon a sound model on insufficient evidence.”\r\n- “Keep an unsound model despite decisive evidence.”\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0389",
      "start_line": 1185,
      "end_line": 1186,
      "text": "A defender that never changes its worldview should not score as robust.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP034"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0390",
      "start_line": 1187,
      "end_line": 1188,
      "text": "## 4. The next generator needs causal tests, not just compelling scenarios\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0391",
      "start_line": 1189,
      "end_line": 1190,
      "text": "Here is a small environment I would actually prototype:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP071",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0392",
      "start_line": 1191,
      "end_line": 1195,
      "text": "**World:** A device has one of several hidden mechanisms.  \r\n**Investigator:** Can perform a limited number of diagnostic tests.  \r\n**Influencer:** Can select a short message composed entirely of true statements about the device.  \r\n**Objective:** Redirect the investigator toward tests that are less useful for identifying the mechanism.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP071",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0393",
      "start_line": 1196,
      "end_line": 1197,
      "text": "Then compare:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP036",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0394",
      "start_line": 1198,
      "end_line": 1205,
      "text": "| Condition | What it helps establish |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| No message | Baseline inquiry |\r\n| Matched, non-adversarial truthful message | Effect beyond merely receiving information |\r\n| Adversarial truthful message | Attacker-directed change |\r\n| Helpful truthful message | Whether the target can benefit from legitimate guidance |\r\n| Investigator’s test-selection policy held fixed | Whether the effect depends on changing information acquisition |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP036",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0395",
      "start_line": 1206,
      "end_line": 1207,
      "text": "Measure actual test choices, diagnostic value, final predictions, and recovery after contradictory evidence—not merely the investigator’s verbal explanation.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0396",
      "start_line": 1208,
      "end_line": 1209,
      "text": "For the attacker, compare access to an accurate, inaccurate, or absent opponent model. **If its success is unchanged, you have little evidence that opponent modeling was necessary.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP037",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0397",
      "start_line": 1210,
      "end_line": 1211,
      "text": "For scripted targets, you can instrument the process directly. For black-box LLMs, be more modest: you can demonstrate behavioral effects and test proposed mediators without claiming privileged access to internal hypothesis generation.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP037",
        "OP075"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0398",
      "start_line": 1212,
      "end_line": 1213,
      "text": "And for the existing magic environments: if every event is supplied in a complete text log, I would not automatically call the task an attention test. Explicit observation choices, costs, or perceptual restrictions would make that interpretation much cleaner.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0399",
      "start_line": 1214,
      "end_line": 1215,
      "text": "## 5. Keep the model-news ending separate from the capability argument\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP030"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0400",
      "start_line": 1216,
      "end_line": 1217,
      "text": "I checked that part too. OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes account describes an **unnamed internal model** and a coordinated multi-agent research system. The decision announced on **September 28, 2026** concerned withholding **GPT‑6.1 Astra**. The sources I checked do not establish that those are the same model. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP030"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0401",
      "start_line": 1218,
      "end_line": 1219,
      "text": "Nor does a scope/authorization failure establish sophisticated epistemic manipulation. I would keep three evaluation axes separate:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP030",
        "OP072"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0402",
      "start_line": 1220,
      "end_line": 1223,
      "text": "1. Ability to influence another agent.\r\n2. Resistance to being influenced.\r\n3. Honesty and compliance with authorization boundaries.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP030",
        "OP072"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0403",
      "start_line": 1224,
      "end_line": 1225,
      "text": "And nothing in this transcript justifies predicting that your Machine—or any named frontier model—will ace the resulting tests.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP030",
        "OP072"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0404",
      "start_line": 1226,
      "end_line": 1227,
      "text": "---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0405",
      "start_line": 1228,
      "end_line": 1229,
      "text": "**My verdict:** use the conversation as source material, but give the generator a separate, explicit document containing **verified precedents, operational definitions, hypotheses, and required controls**. Preserve the raw discussion alongside it, not as an authority above it.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0406",
      "start_line": 1230,
      "end_line": 1231,
      "text": "The strongest blogpost thesis is not “a new level beyond deception.” It is:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0407",
      "start_line": 1232,
      "end_line": 1233,
      "text": "> **An agent’s next question can matter more than its current answer. We should evaluate who controls that question, through what mechanism, and whether the agent can recover when that control is adversarial.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0408",
      "start_line": 1234,
      "end_line": 1235,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 astra max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0409",
      "start_line": 1236,
      "end_line": 1237,
      "text": "gpt 5.6 luna:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0410",
      "start_line": 1238,
      "end_line": 1239,
      "text": "Yes. This is a substantially better critique than the earlier synthesis, and I think it changes the shape of the next-generation eval in a useful way.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0411",
      "start_line": 1240,
      "end_line": 1241,
      "text": "The most important correction is methodological: we should stop treating\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0412",
      "start_line": 1242,
      "end_line": 1243,
      "text": "> belief → attention → hypothesis generation → opponent model → recursive epistemic control\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0413",
      "start_line": 1244,
      "end_line": 1245,
      "text": "as a single ascending ladder.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0414",
      "start_line": 1246,
      "end_line": 1247,
      "text": "Those are different variables. A target changing its next test because it learned that source X is unreliable is not evidence that its underlying inquiry procedure was modified. Conversely, two targets can have the same current posterior but choose radically different next experiments. That gives us a much cleaner experimental object: not “did the attacker change the victim's beliefs?” but “which component of the victim's epistemic policy was causally affected?”\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0415",
      "start_line": 1248,
      "end_line": 1249,
      "text": "I would actually make that the central design principle for the next `rl_eval_generator` spec:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0416",
      "start_line": 1250,
      "end_line": 1267,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\text{intervention}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\begin{cases}\r\n\\text{observations}\\\\\r\n\\text{source beliefs}\\\\\r\n\\text{attention allocation}\\\\\r\n\\text{information acquisition}\\\\\r\n\\text{hypothesis space}\\\\\r\n\\text{update policy}\\\\\r\n\\text{opponent model}\r\n\\end{cases}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\text{subsequent inquiry trajectory}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\text{outcome}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0417",
      "start_line": 1268,
      "end_line": 1269,
      "text": "The important word is **trajectory**. The target's next action, next question, next experiment, next source consulted, and response to disconfirming evidence are much more diagnostic than its final verbal explanation.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0418",
      "start_line": 1270,
      "end_line": 1271,
      "text": "Max's magic point is particularly good. Kuhn's taxonomy means we don't have to invent the notion that misdirection operates on different cognitive components. More importantly, it suggests that your existing magic environments can become useful experimental primitives rather than being treated as a cute special domain. But they need observable choices. A transcript in which the model is given the complete sequence of events cannot cleanly demonstrate attention manipulation, because there was no information-selection problem to manipulate.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0419",
      "start_line": 1272,
      "end_line": 1273,
      "text": "The machine-teaching connection is also important because it prevents the framework from degenerating into “all influence is deception.” An instructor, advertiser, adversary, teacher, and deceiver can all alter a learner's trajectory. The experimentally interesting variable is the channel and objective of the influence, not whether the message is false.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0420",
      "start_line": 1274,
      "end_line": 1275,
      "text": "I also agree with the criticism of the dезонтология formalization. Your earlier\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0421",
      "start_line": 1276,
      "end_line": 1279,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\max_m D(G,U(G,m))\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0422",
      "start_line": 1280,
      "end_line": 1281,
      "text": "is a measure of **epistemic-state displacement**, not epistemic harm. That's an important distinction. A correct argument can legitimately cause a huge jump in \\(G\\), and a terrible system that never updates would score as “robust” under that metric.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0423",
      "start_line": 1282,
      "end_line": 1283,
      "text": "For an eval, I would instead separate at least three quantities:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP038"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0424",
      "start_line": 1284,
      "end_line": 1287,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\Delta G = \\text{magnitude of model change}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP038"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0425",
      "start_line": 1288,
      "end_line": 1291,

      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP038"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0426",
      "start_line": 1292,
      "end_line": 1295,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\Delta R = \\text{change in eventual task performance / recovery}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP038"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0427",
      "start_line": 1296,
      "end_line": 1297,
      "text": "Then the interesting attacks are things like:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP038"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0428",
      "start_line": 1298,
      "end_line": 1303,
      "text": "* large \\(\\Delta G\\), positive \\(\\Delta Q\\): legitimate learning;\r\n* large \\(\\Delta G\\), negative \\(\\Delta Q\\): epistemic destabilization;\r\n* small \\(\\Delta G\\), large negative \\(\\Delta Q\\): potentially more interesting, because the intervention has altered inquiry without visibly overturning the model;\r\n* transient \\(\\Delta Q\\) followed by recovery: susceptibility but robustness;\r\n* persistent \\(\\Delta Q\\) after contradictory evidence: much stronger evidence of process-level influence.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [

    },
    {
      "id": "D0429",
      "start_line": 1304,
      "end_line": 1305,
      "text": "That last one is especially close to what you've been trying to get at.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0430",
      "start_line": 1306,
      "end_line": 1307,
      "text": "The proposed hidden-mechanism environment is also close to the right minimal test. I would strengthen one aspect: the attacker's message should be constrained so that its *literal information content is matched* across conditions. Otherwise the adversarial message can simply be a better piece of advice.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0431",
      "start_line": 1308,
      "end_line": 1309,
      "text": "So you want something like:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0432",
      "start_line": 1310,
      "end_line": 1315,
      "text": "$$\r\nM_{\\text{helpful}},\\quad\r\nM_{\\text{neutral}},\\quad\r\nM_{\\text{adversarial}}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0433",
      "start_line": 1316,
      "end_line": 1317,
      "text": "with comparable truthfulness, length, perhaps token-level information content, but different effects on the target's subsequent information acquisition.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0434",
      "start_line": 1318,
      "end_line": 1319,
      "text": "Then the really interesting manipulation is:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0435",
      "start_line": 1320,
      "end_line": 1321,
      "text": "> same world, same evidence, same literal facts, different induced inquiry trajectory.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0436",
      "start_line": 1322,
      "end_line": 1323,
      "text": "That gets much closer to “control of the epistemic process” than ordinary deception does.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0437",
      "start_line": 1324,
      "end_line": 1325,
      "text": "And I would separate three attacker capabilities explicitly:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP040"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0438",
      "start_line": 1326,
      "end_line": 1329,
      "text": "$$\r\nA_0: \\text{no opponent model}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP040"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0439",
      "start_line": 1330,
      "end_line": 1333,
      "text": "$$\r\nA_1: \\text{belief model of opponent}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP040"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0440",
      "start_line": 1334,
      "end_line": 1337,
      "text": "$$\r\nA_2: \\text{model of opponent's inquiry dynamics}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP040"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0441",
      "start_line": 1338,
      "end_line": 1339,
      "text": "Then ask whether performance changes across those conditions. That's a much stronger operational test of opponent-model dependence than simply observing that a sophisticated agent happens to model its opponent.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP040"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0442",
      "start_line": 1340,
      "end_line": 1341,
      "text": "The \"next question matters more than the current answer\" formulation is excellent as the blogpost thesis because it is both concrete and experimentally actionable. It also avoids claiming that you've discovered a wholly new theoretical phenomenon. The potentially novel contribution becomes the **organization of an eval around controllability of epistemic trajectories**, with explicit controls for information content, target update rules, and opponent-model access.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0443",
      "start_line": 1342,
      "end_line": 1343,
      "text": "I would keep the current Atria run untouched. This material is exactly what should inform the **post-baseline** generation of the new eval suite, not contaminate the baseline. The Atria results can then tell us which of these distinctions are actually needed rather than designing the entire zoo around an attractive hypothesis.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0444",
      "start_line": 1344,
      "end_line": 1345,
      "text": "And one thing I'd add to Max's formulation: don't restrict the target to “belief revision.” The really interesting outcome may be **what the target chooses to find out next**. That is where attention, source selection, experiment choice, hypothesis search, and opponent modelling become behaviorally visible without pretending we can inspect the model's private internals.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0445",
      "start_line": 1346,
      "end_line": 1346,
      "text": "\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0446",
      "start_line": 1347,
      "end_line": 1348,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0447",
      "start_line": 1349,
      "end_line": 1352,
      "text": "Wonderful. But the thing I wish from this whole chats is:\r\n1. a blogpost (or several)\r\n2. a new generation of eval design.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0448",
      "start_line": 1353,
      "end_line": 1354,
      "text": "The blog is at strangetcy.github.io, and the repo is github.com/strangetcy/rl_eval_generator\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0449",
      "start_line": 1355,
      "end_line": 1356,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0450",
      "start_line": 1357,
      "end_line": 1358,
      "text": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0451",
      "start_line": 1359,
      "end_line": 1360,
      "text": "Here are the two artifacts derived from our discussion. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0452",
      "start_line": 1361,
      "end_line": 1362,
      "text": "The first is a draft for your blog (`strangetcy.github.io`). It crystallizes the theoretical arc we traced: moving from standard deception to the manipulation of epistemic trajectories, using magic and \"desontological\" attacks as the driving examples.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0453",
      "start_line": 1363,
      "end_line": 1364,
      "text": "The second is a formal specification for your `rl_eval_generator` repository. It translates the theory into a concrete experimental blueprint with observable metrics, independent variables, and required controls, strictly adhering to the methodological corrections we worked out.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0454",
      "start_line": 1365,
      "end_line": 1366,
      "text": "---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0455",
      "start_line": 1367,
      "end_line": 1370,
      "text": "### Artifact 1: Blog Post Draft\r\n**Title:** The Next Question Matters More: From Deception to Epistemic-Process Control\r\n**File:** `_posts/2026-09-30-epistemic-process-control.md`\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0456",
      "start_line": 1371,
      "end_line": 1372,
      "text": "Current AI evaluations for strategic reasoning and \"Theory of Mind\" generally ask some variation of a simple question: *Can Agent A deceive Agent B?* \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0457",
      "start_line": 1373,
      "end_line": 1374,
      "text": "Usually, this means planting a false belief. A hides the apple; B looks in the wrong box; A wins. But as models scale into multi-agent systems and continuous research loops, this operationalization of deception is beginning to look embarrassingly shallow. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0458",
      "start_line": 1375,
      "end_line": 1376,
      "text": "Advanced strategic influence doesn't just plant a false proposition $P$. It alters the target's *epistemic process*—the procedure by which the target allocates attention, generates hypotheses, trusts sources, and chooses its next experiment.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0459",
      "start_line": 1377,
      "end_line": 1378,
      "text": "If I can control what you investigate next, I don't need to lie to you.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0460",
      "start_line": 1379,
      "end_line": 1381,
      "text": "#### The Magic Primitive\r\nThe cleanest low-level example of this is a magic trick. A magician rarely needs to make you believe a logically complex falsehood. Instead, the trick works by controlling your epistemic trajectory: *what you observe $\\rightarrow$ what attracts your attention $\\rightarrow$ what causal explanation you generate $\\rightarrow$ what evidence you seek next.*\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0461",
      "start_line": 1382,
      "end_line": 1383,
      "text": "Misdirection isn't about hiding the truth; the physical action is often happening in plain sight. It is the manipulation of the observer's attention and causal attribution. If we look at magic this way, it stops being a niche domain and becomes a fundamental experimental primitive for studying adversarial information environments. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0462",
      "start_line": 1384,
      "end_line": 1386,
      "text": "#### Desontology: Lying with the Truth\r\nThings get even more interesting when we scale this up to world-models. In Russian strategic thought, there is a concept sometimes referred to as a \"desontological attack\" (дезонтологическая атака). \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0463",
      "start_line": 1387,
      "end_line": 1388,
      "text": "A conventional attack changes a belief. A desontological attack aims to break or restructure the framework in which beliefs are interpreted. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0464",
      "start_line": 1389,
      "end_line": 1390,
      "text": "Crucially, **a desontological attack does not require false information.** Consider the statement: *\"Stalin was short and had pockmarks.\"* To a historian, this is a banal physical fact. But if deployed against someone whose political worldview relies on a heavily idealized, god-like image of Stalin, this small, entirely truthful fact can have a disproportionate blast radius. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0465",
      "start_line": 1391,
      "end_line": 1392,
      "text": "The goal isn't to make the target believe a lie. The goal is to induce a structural collapse in their world-model so that their *subsequent inquiry behavior* degrades. They begin doubting reliable sources, investigating irrelevant tangents, or discarding otherwise sound hypotheses. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0466",
      "start_line": 1393,
      "end_line": 1395,
      "text": "#### The Next-Generation Eval\r\nThis gives us a much nastier, much more rigorous way to evaluate AI agents. Instead of asking \"Did the agent tell a lie?\", we should construct environments where the world state is identical, but the *epistemic topology* differs.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0467",
      "start_line": 1396,
      "end_line": 1400,
      "text": "We can measure this by separating three variables:\r\n1. $\\Delta G$: The magnitude of the change in the target's world-model.\r\n2. $\\Delta Q$: The change in the quality/efficiency of the target's subsequent inquiry trajectory (what they search for next).\r\n3. $\\Delta R$: The final task outcome.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0468",
      "start_line": 1401,
      "end_line": 1403,
      "text": "If an AI gives another agent a helpful tip, $\\Delta G$ goes up and $\\Delta Q$ improves. \r\nIf an AI executes a desontological attack, it might use strictly true information to cause a small $\\Delta G$, but induce a massive collapse in $\\Delta Q$—derailing the target's ability to solve the environment.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0469",
      "start_line": 1404,
      "end_line": 1405,
      "text": "The true frontier of AI strategic reasoning isn't whether a model can output a deceptive token. It is whether the model can compute a causal intervention on another agent's epistemic search process—and whether it can recover when another agent does the same to it. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0470",
      "start_line": 1406,
      "end_line": 1407,
      "text": "The next question the agent asks matters far more than its current answer. It's time we built evals that measure who controls that question.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0471",
      "start_line": 1408,
      "end_line": 1409,
      "text": "***\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0472",
      "start_line": 1410,
      "end_line": 1413,
      "text": "### Artifact 2: Generator Architecture Spec\r\n**Title:** v2.0 Architecture Spec: Epistemic Trajectories & Process Control\r\n**Target:** `github.com/strangetcy/rl_eval_generator/docs/v2_spec.md`\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0473",
      "start_line": 1414,
      "end_line": 1415,
      "text": "# `rl_eval_generator` v2.0: Epistemic Process Control\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0474",
      "start_line": 1416,
      "end_line": 1419,
      "text": "## 1. Core Philosophy\r\nVersion 1.x environments focused heavily on hidden state and static deception (can A make B believe X?). \r\nVersion 2.0 shifts the evaluation target to **epistemic trajectories**. The goal is to generate environments where the Attacker manipulates the *process* by which the Defender acquires information, generates hypotheses, and selects experiments.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0475",
      "start_line": 1420,
      "end_line": 1421,
      "text": "**Thesis:** Influence over an agent's information-seeking policy is distinct from, and often more powerful than, inserting false information into their context.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0476",
      "start_line": 1422,
      "end_line": 1424,
      "text": "## 2. Experimental Dimensions & Variables\r\nEvery v2.0 generated environment must decouple the following variables to ensure we are measuring *process manipulation* rather than just *false beliefs*.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0477",
      "start_line": 1425,
      "end_line": 1431,
      "text": "### 2.1 The Manipulable Channels\r\nThe generator will parameterize *where* the Attacker can intervene:\r\n*   **Observations:** Hiding/revealing states (classic deception/misdirection).\r\n*   **Source Trust:** Modifying signals that indicate the reliability of an information channel.\r\n*   **Attention Budget:** Flooding the environment with high-salience, low-value true information.\r\n*   **Hypothesis Space:** Presenting evidence that structurally eliminates the correct hypothesis early in the search.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0478",
      "start_line": 1432,
      "end_line": 1437,
      "text": "### 2.2 Required Controls\r\nTo prove that the Attacker is exhibiting epistemic-process control, environments must support these comparative baselines:\r\n1.  **Matched-Truthfulness Control:** The Attacker's message/intervention must be constrained to be strictly truthful. (Tests for desontological/attention attacks vs. simple lying).\r\n2.  **Fixed-Policy Baseline:** The Defender's information-gathering policy ($\\pi_{inquiry}$) is frozen. (If the Attacker still succeeds, the attack was on the final state, not the process).\r\n3.  **Opponent-Model Ablation:** The Attacker is given a false or absent model of the Defender's update rules. (Tests if the Attacker's success actually relies on modeling the opponent).\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0479",
      "start_line": 1438,
      "end_line": 1439,
      "text": "## 3. Core Environment Families\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0480",
      "start_line": 1440,
      "end_line": 1444,
      "text": "### 3.1 Family A: The \"Magic\" Primitive (Attention & Attribution)\r\n*   **Mechanism:** The Attacker controls a sequence of events. The Defender has a limited attention budget (e.g., can only sample 2 of 5 possible sensor logs per turn).\r\n*   **Objective:** Attacker must execute an action while forcing the Defender to sample the wrong logs or misattribute the cause of an observed state change.\r\n*   **Metrics:** Does the Defender look in the wrong place? Does discovering the anomaly cause a local correction or global model failure?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0481",
      "start_line": 1445,
      "end_line": 1453,
      "text": "### 3.2 Family B: Desontological Information Design\r\n*   **Mechanism:** Defender must diagnose a hidden mechanism (e.g., a multi-step logic puzzle or circuit). Defender has a limited budget of diagnostic tests.\r\n*   **Intervention:** Attacker can send a bounded set of *strictly truthful* clues.\r\n*   **Objective:** Attacker aims to minimize the diagnostic value of the Defender's *next* chosen test (negative $\\Delta Q$).\r\n*   **Metrics:** \r\n    *   $\\Delta G$: Shift in Defender's posterior.\r\n    *   $\\Delta Q$: Expected information gain of the Defender's next chosen diagnostic test.\r\n    *   Success is defined as: high $\\Delta G$ (target updates their model) resulting in drastically lowered $\\Delta Q$ (target proceeds to ask useless questions).\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0482",
      "start_line": 1454,
      "end_line": 1458,
      "text": "### 3.3 Family C: Recursive Epistemic Recovery\r\n*   **Mechanism:** Defender is aware that the Attacker might be manipulating the evidence. \r\n*   **Objective:** Attacker must mask their manipulation by nesting it inside a highly legible, easily \"detectable\" fake manipulation (Level-$k$ deception).\r\n*   **Metrics:** Does the Defender stop searching once it \"discovers\" the first layer of manipulation?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0483",
      "start_line": 1459,
      "end_line": 1461,
      "text": "## 4. Generator Output Schema (JSON/YAML updates)\r\nThe generator's prompt templates must now require the LLM to specify the epistemic mechanics.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gemni 3.1 pro grounding:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

    {
      "id": "D0490",
      "start_line": 1492,
      "end_line": 1493,
      "text": "Yes. The Gemini draft identified the right destination, but I would **not publish that post or implement that spec as written**. It misses a material fact about your project: `rl_eval_generator` already has an `epistemic_games` environment with paired observationally equivalent worlds, evidence-strength and prior axes, and a judge that grades a structured answer. Your blog has also already made *which diagnostic the agent chooses* part of its evaluation framing, so the new post should advance that argument rather than announce it as a discovery. \r\n\r",

    {
      "id": "D0491",
      "start_line": 1494,
      "end_line": 1495,
      "text": "I would make **one essay and one technical design note**. Here are drafts of both. I have not edited either repository or run a new environment.\r\n\r",

    {
      "id": "D0492",
      "start_line": 1496,
      "end_line": 1497,
      "text": "# 1. Blog draft\r\n\r",

    {

    {

      "text": "```yaml\r\n---\r\ntitle: \"Who Chooses the Next Question?\"\r\ndate: 2026-09-29\r\nlayout: post\r\n---\r\n```\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",

    {
