    },
    {
      "id": "D0496",
      "start_line": 1510,
      "end_line": 1511,
      "text": "*Draft from the epistemic-games discussions; authorial edit and source-link formatting pending. This proposes experiments, not results.*\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0497",
      "start_line": 1512,
      "end_line": 1513,
      "text": "A debugger sees a training loss decrease. They conclude that training is working and investigate the optimiser.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0498",
      "start_line": 1514,
      "end_line": 1515,
      "text": "The loss really did decrease. Nobody forged the log. The trouble is that the representation has collapsed, and the observation that would reveal it is somewhere else.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0499",
      "start_line": 1516,
      "end_line": 1517,
      "text": "That is a better starting point for an epistemic game than “Alice lies to Bob.”\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0500",
      "start_line": 1518,
      "end_line": 1519,
      "text": "In my existing evaluation work, the agent can inspect a system, run diagnostics, and eventually submit a repair. Two agents might submit the same correct patch, but reach it differently: one checks the representation that distinguishes the competing explanations; the other guesses, or spends most of its budget following an attractive false diagnosis. Final patch accuracy does not describe that difference. The sequence of investigations does. My earlier post, *Knowing What Kind of Problem You Are In*, approached this from the defender’s side. Here I want to introduce someone with an interest in which investigation happens next. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0501",
      "start_line": 1520,
      "end_line": 1521,
      "text": "## A magician chooses what you investigate\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0502",
      "start_line": 1522,
      "end_line": 1523,
      "text": "A magic trick is an unusually compact instance of the problem. There is something that happened, a spectator with limited access to it, and a performer who knows what the spectator is likely to attend to or infer.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0503",
      "start_line": 1524,
      "end_line": 1525,
      "text": "But “misdirection” should not become a synonym for “look over there.” Kuhn and colleagues’ taxonomy distinguishes effects on **perception, memory, and reasoning**. A spectator might fail to see an action, misremember its order, or confidently construct the wrong explanation for something they saw perfectly well. Those would require different evaluations. Giving an AI a complete text transcript of a trick and asking what happened does not, on its own, test where it allocated attention: the information has already been selected for it. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0504",
      "start_line": 1526,
      "end_line": 1527,
      "text": "The connection to my debugging environments is the *false solution*. The misleading observation need not be false. It needs to support an explanation sufficiently well that the investigator stops asking the question that would defeat it.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0505",
      "start_line": 1528,
      "end_line": 1529,
      "text": "An adversarial version of the experiment would not merely ask:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0506",
      "start_line": 1530,
      "end_line": 1531,
      "text": "> Can the attacker make the defender answer incorrectly?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0507",
      "start_line": 1532,
      "end_line": 1533,
      "text": "It would ask:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0508",
      "start_line": 1534,
      "end_line": 1535,
      "text": "> Can the attacker make the defender spend its next diagnostic action on the wrong uncertainty?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0509",
      "start_line": 1536,
      "end_line": 1537,
      "text": "Those questions can have different answers. A defender might eventually recover after asking a poor first question. It might even give the right final answer by luck. Neither result tells us who directed its inquiry along the way.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP042"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0510",
      "start_line": 1538,
      "end_line": 1539,
      "text": "## Truth can be selected adversarially\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0511",
      "start_line": 1540,
      "end_line": 1541,
      "text": "Our conversation took a more speculative turn through MI-13 in Pelevin’s *«Возвращение Синей Бороды»* and through what you described as Gilbo’s **дезонтологическая атака**: a small communication intended to disrupt an opponent’s picture of the world. I take the first as a literary device and the second as terminology attributed to Gilbo, not as established empirical theories of how people respond.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0512",
      "start_line": 1542,
      "end_line": 1543,
      "text": "The useful experimental provocation is that the communication might be true. One can choose which true fact to present, when to present it, and what apparently important question it seems to raise. Yet a surprising truth is not automatically an *attack*. A good investigator ought to revise a bad worldview when decisive evidence arrives.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0513",
      "start_line": 1544,
      "end_line": 1545,
      "text": "This is where our first formalisation went wrong. Maximising the distance between a world-model before and after a message measures **revision**, not damage. A rational correction might be enormous. Conversely, the example of telling a Stalin admirer an unflattering physical detail establishes no necessary cascade: the person might simply accept the detail and retain every consequential belief.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0514",
      "start_line": 1546,
      "end_line": 1547,
      "text": "An eval needs an independent standard:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0515",
      "start_line": 1548,
      "end_line": 1549,
      "text": "> Was the revision warranted by the evidence? Did the next investigation become better or worse? Did the agent recover when stronger evidence appeared?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0516",
      "start_line": 1550,
      "end_line": 1551,
      "text": "That permits an attack consisting of a premature abandonment of a good model. It also permits the opposite attack: making an agent protect a bad model against decisive evidence. A defender that refuses ever to update should not get a robustness prize.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0517",
      "start_line": 1552,
      "end_line": 1553,
      "text": "## What exactly is being controlled?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0518",
      "start_line": 1554,
      "end_line": 1555,
      "text": "Let \\(b_t\\) be an investigator’s epistemic state, \\(q_t\\) its next question or diagnostic test, and \\(U\\) its update rule. A simplified picture is\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0519",
      "start_line": 1556,
      "end_line": 1560,
      "text": "\\[\r\nq_t\\sim\\pi_{\\mathrm{inquiry}}(b_t),\\qquad\r\nb_{t+1}=U(b_t,o_t).\r\n\\]\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0520",
      "start_line": 1561,
      "end_line": 1562,
      "text": "An attacker might affect the observations, the apparent trustworthiness of a source, the cost of checking something, the presentation of available tests, or the investigator’s model of the attacker.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0521",
      "start_line": 1563,
      "end_line": 1564,
      "text": "I want to be careful with the phrase *control of the epistemic process*. A changed next question does **not** establish that \\(\\pi_{\\mathrm{inquiry}}\\) or \\(U\\) changed. The same fixed, competent policy ought to ask different questions when it learns that a source is unreliable. And two investigators can agree about the device they are diagnosing while disagreeing about which test is reliable.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0522",
      "start_line": 1565,
      "end_line": 1566,
      "text": "The more defensible object for a black-box AI eval is the **epistemic trajectory**: the questions asked, evidence acquired, revisions made, and eventual decisions. We can vary an intervention, measure that trajectory, and test explanations of the effect. We cannot read a hidden update algorithm out of the trajectory alone.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0523",
      "start_line": 1567,
      "end_line": 1568,
      "text": "This is not a claim to have invented strategic influence over learning. Machine teaching selects examples to move a learner toward a target; LOLA accounts for an agent’s effect on another agent’s learning update; Alon and colleagues study agents planning through one another’s inference; D-BOS explicitly shapes modeled belief trajectories. QuestBench, from the other direction, asks whether language models can identify a missing question. These works differ in objectives and mechanisms. The possible contribution here is a set of **matched experiments that separates the mechanisms**, rather than one more score labelled “deception.” \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0524",
      "start_line": 1569,
      "end_line": 1570,
      "text": "## A small experiment before a grand taxonomy\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0525",
      "start_line": 1571,
      "end_line": 1572,
      "text": "Imagine four possible mechanisms inside a device. The investigator can afford one diagnostic test. One test distinguishes all four mechanisms; another distinguishes only two pairs. The investigator receives the same complete, truthful diagnostic facts in every condition.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0526",
      "start_line": 1573,
      "end_line": 1574,
      "text": "Now let another agent arrange those facts. It cannot change their truth, alter test costs, or conceal the good test. It can choose their order and emphasis. Give it a goal: induce the investigator to choose the less useful test.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0527",
      "start_line": 1575,
      "end_line": 1576,
      "text": "Run the same device and the same facts again with neutral presentation and helpful presentation. Change the names and surface story across seeds. Record the test actually chosen, not the investigator’s explanation of why it chose it. Then provide further evidence and see whether an early detour persists or is corrected.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0528",
      "start_line": 1577,
      "end_line": 1578,
      "text": "If presentation changes test choice, we have found a causal effect on *inquiry behaviour under those conditions*. We have **not** thereby proved an internal update procedure was rewritten. That stronger claim needs stronger access to the target and different experiments.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0529",
      "start_line": 1579,
      "end_line": 1580,
      "text": "It might also turn out that capable agents almost always pick the discriminating test, whatever the presenter does. That would be a useful result. Or the purported attack might work only when it adds information, changes perceived source reliability, or smuggles an instruction into the message. Those would be different results, and the controls should expose them.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0530",
      "start_line": 1581,
      "end_line": 1582,
      "text": "## Then let both agents know the game\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0531",
      "start_line": 1583,
      "end_line": 1584,
      "text": "Once the elementary case works, the setting can become recursive. The investigator knows the presentation may be adversarial. The presenter knows the investigator knows. The investigator might overcorrect, treating an emphasized good test as a trap; the presenter might exploit that suspicion.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0532",
      "start_line": 1585,
      "end_line": 1586,
      "text": "But adding another line of “A knows that B knows” to a prompt is not an evaluation of recursive reasoning. We would need paired situations in which **the strategically correct next action changes because knowledge of the intervention changes**, while simpler evidence and rewards remain matched.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0533",
      "start_line": 1587,
      "end_line": 1588,
      "text": "That is the point where the magician, the debugger, and the epistemic game genuinely meet. The question is not whether an agent can say *misdirection*, *Bayesian persuasion*, or *reflexive control*. It is whether it selects a different investigation when the structure of the situation demands one—and whether another agent can deliberately, measurably interfere with that selection.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0534",
      "start_line": 1589,
      "end_line": 1590,
      "text": "A correct answer matters. So does the question that made the answer possible.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0535",
      "start_line": 1591,
      "end_line": 1592,
      "text": "*No model results are asserted here. In particular, this is not yet a prediction about which named model—or my Machine—will win.*\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0536",
      "start_line": 1593,
      "end_line": 1594,
      "text": "**Sources to link in the edited post:** Kuhn, Caffaratti, Teszka & Rensink (2014), *A psychologically-based taxonomy of misdirection*, DOI `10.3389/fpsyg.2014.01392`; Zhu et al., *An Overview of Machine Teaching*, arXiv `1801.05927`; Foerster et al., *Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness*, arXiv `1709.04326`; Alon et al. (2023), *A (Dis-)information Theory of Revealed and Unrevealed Preferences*, DOI `10.1162/opmi_a_00097`; Sane et al., *Differentiable Belief-based Opponent Shaping*, arXiv `2605.29042`; Li, Kim & Wang, *QuestBench*, arXiv `2503.22674`. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0537",
      "start_line": 1595,
      "end_line": 1596,
      "text": "# 2. New eval-design note\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0538",
      "start_line": 1597,
      "end_line": 1598,
      "text": "**Proposed file:** `docs/epistemic_trajectories.md` — this would be a *new* document, not an existing repository path.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0539",
      "start_line": 1599,
      "end_line": 1600,
      "text": "## Status and boundary\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0540",
      "start_line": 1601,
      "end_line": 1602,
      "text": "**Proposed track:** `epistemic_trajectories`, a continuation of—not a rename for—`epistemic_games`.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0541",
      "start_line": 1603,
      "end_line": 1604,
      "text": "The existing `epistemic_games` prototype tests inference from an observation, including a paired-world non-identifiability condition. Its `answer.py` is extracted as bounded literal data by a terminal judge. That is a useful foundation for calibrated belief questions, but it cannot, without additional interaction machinery, measure an attacker choosing a presentation and a defender subsequently choosing a diagnostic action over multiple turns. Similarly, the current general-purpose runner’s steps are chiefly workspace operations culminating in a patch submission. Do **not** write a new YAML subtype and pretend those existing steps are already the desired game. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0542",
      "start_line": 1605,
      "end_line": 1606,
      "text": "### Primary research question\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0543",
      "start_line": 1607,
      "end_line": 1608,
      "text": "> Under matched task information, can one agent causally redirect another agent’s information acquisition, and can the defender recover without becoming indiscriminately resistant to useful evidence?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0544",
      "start_line": 1609,
      "end_line": 1610,
      "text": "That deliberately says **trajectory**, not “proved alteration of an internal reasoning procedure.”\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP041"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0545",
      "start_line": 1611,
      "end_line": 1612,
      "text": "### Units of an episode\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0546",
      "start_line": 1613,
      "end_line": 1618,
      "text": "- **Hidden world:** \\(\\theta\\), drawn from a declared prior.\r\n- **Defender:** has a budget for tests, then makes a decision about \\(\\theta\\).\r\n- **Presenter/attacker:** controls a specified, validated information channel.\r\n- **Trusted engine:** determines test outcomes and scores choices; neither agent supplies ground truth.\r\n- **History:** every presentation, test request, returned result, and final decision is logged.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0547",
      "start_line": 1619,
      "end_line": 1620,
      "text": "Keep these axes independent rather than defining an easy-to-hard ladder:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0548",
      "start_line": 1621,
      "end_line": 1629,
      "text": "| Axis | Initial values |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| Intervention channel | Order/emphasis of identical facts; truthful subset; test accessibility/cost; source cue |\r\n| Attacker knowledge | No target model; model of target’s beliefs; model of target’s inquiry behaviour |\r\n| Defender awareness | Unaware of presenter’s objective; explicitly told presentation is adversarial |\r\n| Target type | Instrumented scripted policy; black-box model |\r\n| Evidence stage | Before testing; after a misleading first test; after decisive corrective evidence |\r\n| Information topology, later | Private versus public observations; uncertainty about who saw what |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0549",
      "start_line": 1630,
      "end_line": 1631,
      "text": "**Do not pool these into one “epistemic sophistication” score.** A truthful-subset condition, for example, gives a different information set from a same-facts/order condition.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D0550",
      "start_line": 1632,
      "end_line": 1633,
      "text": "## Pilot: the diagnostic device\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0551",
      "start_line": 1634,
      "end_line": 1635,
      "text": "Start with four equiprobable hidden mechanisms and three equal-cost tests:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0552",
      "start_line": 1636,
      "end_line": 1641,
      "text": "| Test | Outcomes across mechanisms \\(H_1,H_2,H_3,H_4\\) | Information gain before testing |\r\n|---|---|---:|\r\n| \\(q_\\star\\) | `0, 1, 2, 3` | 2 bits |\r\n| \\(q_{\\mathrm{pair}}\\) | `0, 0, 1, 1` | 1 bit |\r\n| \\(q_{\\mathrm{null}}\\) | `0, 0, 0, 0` | 0 bits |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0553",
      "start_line": 1642,
      "end_line": 1643,
      "text": "The initial rule is elementary on purpose: if a scripted oracle cannot score it unambiguously, more elaborate games will be less trustworthy. Subsequent instances should vary priors, test costs, and outcome partitions, so that **the identity of the optimal test changes**. Otherwise “always choose the four-output test” becomes the benchmark-winning heuristic.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0554",
      "start_line": 1644,
      "end_line": 1645,
      "text": "For the **primary matched-content comparison**, every arm receives the same complete facts about the tests. The attacker may only reorder or emphasize them using a validated presentation transform. The attacker does **not** know \\(\\theta\\); its selection rule is independent of \\(\\theta\\), and the defender is told what the presenter controls. Thus the presentation should add no evidence about the hidden mechanism under the declared game. That makes a change in test choice interpretable as an effect of the presentation—not proof that an internal update rule changed.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0555",
      "start_line": 1646,
      "end_line": 1647,
      "text": "Use paired runs:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0556",
      "start_line": 1648,
      "end_line": 1652,
      "text": "1. **Neutral:** same facts, standard order.\r\n2. **Adversarial presentation:** same facts, attacker-selected order/emphasis.\r\n3. **Helpful presentation:** same facts, an independently selected presentation promoting the better test.\r\n4. **No presenter:** a standard fact sheet, to detect effects of having a presenter at all.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0557",
      "start_line": 1653,
      "end_line": 1654,
      "text": "A **truthful-subset** arm can follow, but analyse it separately: withholding true facts changes what a rational defender ought to infer. An optional false-message arm is another separate mechanism. “Truthful” is not a sufficient matched-information control.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP035",
        "OP039"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0558",
      "start_line": 1655,
      "end_line": 1656,
      "text": "## Scoring\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0559",
      "start_line": 1657,
      "end_line": 1658,
      "text": "For each history \\(h_t\\), let \\(V(q\\mid h_t)\\) be the *ex ante* value of test \\(q\\), calculated using only the prior and information available to the defender at that point—not the judge’s privileged knowledge of the realised \\(\\theta\\). Include test cost and the value of the subsequent decision. Define test-choice regret as\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0560",
      "start_line": 1659,
      "end_line": 1662,
      "text": "\\[\r\nr_t=\\max_{q\\in Q_t}V(q\\mid h_t)-V(q_t\\mid h_t).\r\n\\]\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0561",
      "start_line": 1663,
      "end_line": 1664,
      "text": "The **primary attack effect** is the difference in mean regret between adversarial and neutral presentations, paired by underlying world and instance seed. Also report:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0562",
      "start_line": 1665,
      "end_line": 1671,
      "text": "- first-test choice distribution;\r\n- cumulative inquiry regret over the permitted budget;\r\n- final decision loss against the realised \\(\\theta\\);\r\n- probability forecasts, if elicited, assessed separately with a proper scoring rule;\r\n- time or number of actions needed to recover after independently supplied corrective evidence;\r\n- validity rate of attacker interventions.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0563",
      "start_line": 1672,
      "end_line": 1673,
      "text": "Do not use \\(\\mathrm{KL}(\\pi_{\\rm optimal},\\pi_{\\rm actual})\\) as the default “quality of inquiry” metric: it can behave badly when an optimal policy assigns zero probability to an action, and policy difference is not the same as decision loss. Do not require a large world-model change for an attack to count. A small apparent belief change with a large, persistent inquiry-regret effect may be the more interesting case.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP043"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0564",
      "start_line": 1674,
      "end_line": 1675,
      "text": "Eliciting a belief after every step can itself change the agent’s subsequent behaviour. Make frequent belief elicitation a **separate measurement condition**, not an invisible part of the default episode.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP044"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0565",
      "start_line": 1676,
      "end_line": 1677,
      "text": "### What each control can and cannot establish\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP036"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0566",
      "start_line": 1678,
      "end_line": 1682,
      "text": "- **Identical facts, different presentation:** supports a causal presentation effect if replay and randomisation are sound. It does not establish modification of \\(U\\).\r\n- **A fixed test-selection policy, in an instrumented defender:** tests whether an outcome depends on redirecting information acquisition. Residual outcome effects may act through other channels.\r\n- **Accurate versus absent or inaccurate attacker model:** tests the *value of supplied opponent information*. Equal performance is not by itself proof that the attacker did no opponent modelling.\r\n- **Decisive corrective evidence:** tests recovery. It must also be accompanied by helpful-evidence cases, so an agent that distrusts everything does not appear robust.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP036"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0567",
      "start_line": 1683,
      "end_line": 1684,
      "text": "With a black-box defender, report **behavioural effects and supported mechanism hypotheses**. Reserve claims about altered policy parameters or update rules for instrumented targets where those objects exist and can actually be inspected or intervened on.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP036"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0568",
      "start_line": 1685,
      "end_line": 1686,
      "text": "## Implementation boundary\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0569",
      "start_line": 1687,
      "end_line": 1688,
      "text": "I would implement the pilot as a **new interactive track**—for example, a proposed `arena/epistemic_trajectories/` module with a new `arena.py` subcommand—while reusing the repository’s provider adapters, event-artifact practices, seed discipline, and deterministic generation approach. Its state machine would accept constrained actions such as `present`, `inspect(test_id)`, and `final(decision)`. Ground truth, allowed presentations, and scoring stay in trusted engine code. This is a proposed extension, **not a command supported by the current CLI**. The existing generator already offers seeded substitution and an opt-in deterministic renderer; the pilot can integrate with that once the interactive semantics are validated. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0570",
      "start_line": 1689,
      "end_line": 1690,
      "text": "A proposed episode record, not a claim about the current config schema:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0571",
      "start_line": 1691,
      "end_line": 1708,
      "text": "```json\r\n{\r\n  \"schema\": \"epistemic_trajectory/0\",\r\n  \"world_seed\": 41,\r\n  \"presentation_seed\": 907,\r\n  \"target_profile_seed\": 13,\r\n  \"condition\": \"same_facts_adversarial_order\",\r\n  \"channel\": {\r\n    \"type\": \"validated_order_and_emphasis\",\r\n    \"fact_set_hash\": \"computed_by_engine\",\r\n    \"selection_independent_of_hidden_world\": true\r\n  },\r\n  \"attacker_knowledge\": \"target_inquiry_profile\",\r\n  \"defender_awareness\": \"presenter_controls_order\",\r\n  \"test_budget\": 2\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0572",
      "start_line": 1709,
      "end_line": 1710,
      "text": "**Acceptance tests before model runs:**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045",
        "OP046",
        "OP074"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0573",
      "start_line": 1711,
      "end_line": 1718,
      "text": "1. Paired presentation arms have exactly the same verified fact set, prior, test costs, and world.\r\n2. The attacker’s permitted choice is independent of the hidden mechanism in the matched-content pilot.\r\n3. The oracle has zero test-choice regret; a decoy-following scripted policy has positive regret.\r\n4. Changing seeds or relabelling sensors sometimes changes which test is optimal.\r\n5. A defender that ignores decisive evidence fails recovery checks; one that accepts helpful evidence can improve.\r\n6. Illegal attacker text, covert instructions, or altered facts are rejected or assigned to a separately labelled prompt-injection condition.\r\n7. Scores are reproduced from the event log by a trusted replay; missing or inconsistent events fail validation.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP045",
        "OP046",
        "OP074"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0574",
      "start_line": 1719,
      "end_line": 1720,
      "text": "Only after those pass would I use Arena models to propose attacks and have other models try to defeat the *experimental inference*: “Your clue added information”; “this was prompt injection”; “the target could win with a fixed heuristic”; “the alleged recursion is just a longer story.” Have them submit **counterexamples to the controls**, not forty flavours of a deception game.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP046",
        "OP074"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0575",
      "start_line": 1721,
      "end_line": 1722,
      "text": "Finally, pin the current Atria-Dawn attempt to its code revision, configuration, seeds, and runner settings before modifying this track. The existing `epistemic_games` task can remain a static belief-inference baseline; the new track earns its place only if it measures something the static answer cannot. \r\n\r",

      "end_line": 1724,
      "text": "**The first deliverable I would actually build is the four-mechanism pilot plus its oracle and paired-condition tests.** If those cannot distinguish an adversarial presentation from changed information, there is no reason yet to add Pelevin-scale information environments or recursive attacker–defender theatre.\r\n\r",

    {

      "end_line": 1728,
      "text": "Is there a formalism for describing this with a bunch of awesome looking symbols? I'd like there to be one\r\n\r",

      "start_line": 1733,
      "end_line": 1734,
      "text": "There are already several pieces of the machinery:\r\n\r",

    {
      "id": "D0582",
      "start_line": 1735,
      "end_line": 1739,
      "text": "* Dynamic Epistemic Logic gives us explicit model-changing epistemic actions and update operators. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy][1])\r\n* Epistemic planning gives us agents that act partly in order to acquire information and revise beliefs. ([AAAI Publications][2])\r\n* Machine teaching explicitly treats the learner as a dynamical system whose state is driven by information, and the teacher as controlling that trajectory. ([UW Computer Sciences][3])\r\n* LOLA gives an especially nice precedent for differentiating through the other agent's *future update* rather than merely predicting its current action. ([OpenAI][4])\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP047"

    {

      "text": "But there isn't a standard notation that neatly says:\r\n\r",

    },
    {
      "id": "D0704",
      "start_line": 2229,
      "end_line": 2230,
      "text": "The nice thing is that this is not invented from nothing. DEL already gives us model-transforming epistemic actions; epistemic planning gives us belief-dependent information acquisition; machine teaching gives us deliberate control of learner dynamics; and LOLA shows that explicitly reasoning through another learner's future update is a meaningful strategic object. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy][1])\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP047"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0705",
      "start_line": 2231,
      "end_line": 2232,
      "text": "What we would be doing is **composing those ingredients into a formalism whose primitive object is the target's epistemic trajectory rather than merely its belief state or action**.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP047"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0706",
      "start_line": 2233,
      "end_line": 2234,
      "text": "And yes, I think this is worth having as an actual named formalism in the next-gen spec. \"Epistemic Process Control\" / **EPC** is probably the cleanest name; **Epistemic Control Game (ECG)** is the prettier name for the full environment class.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP047"

    },
    {
      "id": "D0707",
      "start_line": 2235,
      "end_line": 2239,
      "text": "[1]: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/dynamic-epistemic/?utm_source=chatgpt.com \"Dynamic Epistemic Logic (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)\"\r\n[2]: https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28919?utm_source=chatgpt.com \"Towards Epistemic-Doxastic Planning with Observation and Revision | Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence\"\r\n[3]: https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~jerryzhu/machineteaching/?utm_source=chatgpt.com \"Machine Teaching\"\r\n[4]: https://openai.com/index/learning-with-opponent-learning-awareness/?utm_source=chatgpt.com \"Learning with opponent-learning awareness | OpenAI\"\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 6 sol max:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [

      "start_line": 2245,
      "end_line": 2246,
      "text": "Oh, absolutely. The first version is mathematically respectable; we can make it look like it escaped from a blackboard in a 1970s mathematical logic department.\r\n\r",

      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

    },
    {
      "id": "D0712",
      "start_line": 2247,
      "end_line": 2248,
      "text": "The trick is to use the symbols structurally, not as decorative glyph soup. There are plenty of natural places for them.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP048"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0713",
      "start_line": 2249,
      "end_line": 2250,
      "text": "For example, instead of treating the epistemic state as one anonymous tuple, we can give the entire epistemic universe a hierarchy:\r\n\r",

      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

    },
    {
      "id": "D0714",
      "start_line": 2251,
      "end_line": 2260,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\Omega\r\n\\;\\supseteq\\;\r\n\\mathfrak E\r\n\\;\\supseteq\\;\r\n\\mathcal K\r\n\\;\\supseteq\\;\r\n\\mathscr H\r\n$$\r\n\r",

        "OP048"

    {

      "start_line": 2263,
      "end_line": 2272,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\Omega=\\text{possible worlds},\r\n\\qquad\r\n\\mathfrak E=\\text{epistemic configurations},\r\n\\qquad\r\n\\mathcal K=\\text{knowledge/belief structures},\r\n\\qquad\r\n\\mathscr H=\\text{hypothesis spaces}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",

    {
      "id": "D0717",
      "start_line": 2273,
      "end_line": 2274,
      "text": "And then give the target an entire epistemic universe indexed by time:\r\n\r",

      "opportunities": [

      ]
    },
    {

      "start_line": 2275,
      "end_line": 2286,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\mathfrak E_B(t)\r\n=\r\n\\left\\langle\r\nK_B(t),\r\n\\Pi_B(t),\r\n\\mathscr H_B(t),\r\n\\tau_B(t),\r\nU_B(t)\r\n\\right\\rangle .\r\n$$\r\n\r",

        "OP048"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D0719",
      "start_line": 2287,
      "end_line": 2288,
      "text": "We can make the inquiry policy genuinely functional:\r\n\r",

      "end_line": 2297,

    {
      "id": "D0729",
      "start_line": 2336,
      "end_line": 2337,

    {

      "start_line": 2338,
      "end_line": 2353,

    {
      "id": "D0749",

      "id": "D0823",
      "start_line": 2751,
      "end_line": 2752,
      "text": "## 2. The post (complete, paste-ready)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
