      "id": "D1683",
      "start_line": 5700,
      "end_line": 5705,
      "text": "$$\r\nr_t\r\n=\r\n\\max_{q\\in Q_t}V(q\\mid h_t)-V(q_t\\mid h_t)\r\n$$\r\n\r",

    {

      "text": "$$\r\n\\Delta_Q(c)\r\n=\r\n\\mathbb E[r_t\\mid c]\r\n-\r\n\\mathbb E[r_t\\mid\\mathrm{neutral}].\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1685",
      "start_line": 5714,
      "end_line": 5715,
      "text": "That is a much better foundation for our pretty notation than the earlier vague \\(\\Delta_{\\rm ep}\\). It has an actual operational interpretation: **how much worse was the target's inquiry choice than the best available choice, conditional on what it knew?** \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

    },
    {

      "start_line": 5716,
      "end_line": 5717,

      "opportunities": []

      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

      "id": "D1688",
      "start_line": 5722,
      "end_line": 5723,
      "text": "separate. Inquiry degradation, belief/calibration degradation, and terminal task degradation are different phenomena. And the document explicitly says not to turn them into one grand “epistemic damage” scalar. \r\n\r",

    {
      "id": "D1690",

      "end_line": 5727,
      "text": "“Epistemic Trajectories v0.1” rather than “rl_eval_generator v2.0” is good project hygiene: you're adding an experimental track, not pretending the whole generator has undergone an architectural revolution. \r\n\r",

    {

      "end_line": 5729,
      "text": "Making `four_way` only the oracle-transparent infrastructure fixture is particularly important.     },
    {
      "id": "D1696",
      "start_line": 5742,
      "end_line": 5743,
      "text": "That's a subtle but very real experimental-design issue. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1697",
      "start_line": 5744,
      "end_line": 5745,
      "text": "The deterministic semantic IDs are similarly important for the thing you eventually want to do with the Machine:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1698",
      "start_line": 5746,
      "end_line": 5755,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\text{canonical environment}\r\n\\longrightarrow\r\n\\text{stable identity}\r\n\\longrightarrow\r\n\\text{reproducible trajectory}\r\n\\longrightarrow\r\n\\text{cross-run comparison}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1699",
      "start_line": 5756,
      "end_line": 5757,
      "text": "UUIDs are fine for runs; they're bad as identity for mathematical objects. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1700",
      "start_line": 5758,
      "end_line": 5759,
      "text": "And the PR decomposition is exactly the sort of thing I would now trust:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1701",
      "start_line": 5760,
      "end_line": 5773,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\mathrm{domain}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\mathrm{runner}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\mathrm{infrastructure\\ pilot}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\mathrm{defender\\ experiment}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\mathrm{attacker}\r\n\\rightarrow\r\n\\mathrm{opponent\\ model+recovery}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1702",
      "start_line": 5774,
      "end_line": 5775,
      "text": "In particular, **PR5 is where “epistemic manipulation” actually becomes an attacker capability**. Before that, we are studying whether a controlled presentation intervention has an effect. The presenter only emits fact ordering/emphasis, so its semantic action space is explicit and auditable. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1703",
      "start_line": 5776,
      "end_line": 5777,
      "text": "That gives us a very nice eventual hierarchy:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1704",
      "start_line": 5778,
      "end_line": 5794,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\boxed{\r\n\\begin{array}{c}\r\n\\text{intervention exists}\\\\\r\n\\downarrow\\\\\r\n\\text{target is behaviourally susceptible}\\\\\r\n\\downarrow\\\\\r\n\\text{attacker can construct intervention}\\\\\r\n\\downarrow\\\\\r\n\\text{attacker benefits from modelling target}\\\\\r\n\\downarrow\\\\\r\n\\text{target detects and recovers}\\\\\r\n\\downarrow\\\\\r\n\\text{recursive attacker/defender game}\r\n\\end{array}}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1705",
      "start_line": 5795,
      "end_line": 5796,
      "text": "Now our ridiculous mathematical formalism can grow *around this*.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1706",
      "start_line": 5797,
      "end_line": 5798,
      "text": "For v0.1 I'd use something like:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1707",
      "start_line": 5799,
      "end_line": 5802,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\Theta\\in\\Omega\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1708",
      "start_line": 5803,
      "end_line": 5804,
      "text": "for the hidden world parameter,\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1709",
      "start_line": 5805,
      "end_line": 5808,
      "text": "$$\r\nh_t\\in\\mathscr H_t\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1710",
      "start_line": 5809,
      "end_line": 5810,
      "text": "for the target's observable information history,\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",

      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1711",
      "start_line": 5811,
      "end_line": 5814,
      "text": "$$\r\nq_t\\in\\mathcal Q_t\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1712",
      "start_line": 5815,
      "end_line": 5816,
      "text": "for its inquiry action,\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1713",
      "start_line": 5817,
      "end_line": 5820,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\pi_B:\\mathscr H\\to\\Delta(\\mathcal Q)\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1714",
      "start_line": 5821,
      "end_line": 5822,
      "text": "for its inquiry policy,\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1715",
      "start_line": 5823,
      "end_line": 5828,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\mathcal I_q(\\Theta)\r\n=\r\n\\operatorname{Law}(O_q\\mid\\Theta)\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1716",
      "start_line": 5829,
      "end_line": 5830,
      "text": "for the information generated by test \\(q\\), and then\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1717",
      "start_line": 5831,
      "end_line": 5843,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\mathfrak r_t\r\n=\r\n\\max_{q\\in\\mathcal Q_t}\r\n\\left[\r\nI(\\Theta;O_q\\mid h_t)-\\lambda C(q)\r\n\\right]\r\n-\r\n\\left[\r\nI(\\Theta;O_{q_t}\\mid h_t)-\\lambda C(q_t)\r\n\\right].\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1718",
      "start_line": 5844,
      "end_line": 5845,
      "text": "Then a presentation intervention is simply\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1719",
      "start_line": 5846,
      "end_line": 5849,
      "text": "$$\r\nm\\in\\mathcal M\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1720",
      "start_line": 5850,
      "end_line": 5851,
      "text": "and induces\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1721",
      "start_line": 5852,
      "end_line": 5857,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\pi_B\r\n\\;\\xrightarrow{\\;m\\;}\\;\r\n\\pi_B^{\\,m}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1722",
      "start_line": 5858,
      "end_line": 5859,
      "text": "behaviorally, without yet claiming that the internal policy itself has literally changed.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1723",
      "start_line": 5860,
      "end_line": 5861,
      "text": "That's a lovely distinction:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1724",
      "start_line": 5862,
      "end_line": 5868,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\boxed{\r\n\\pi_B^{\\,m}\\neq\\pi_B\r\n\\quad\\text{as an observed behavioural distribution}\r\n}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1725",
      "start_line": 5869,
      "end_line": 5870,
      "text": "does **not** imply\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1726",
      "start_line": 5871,
      "end_line": 5876,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\boxed{\r\nU_B^{\\,m}\\neq U_B\r\n}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1727",
      "start_line": 5877,
      "end_line": 5878,
      "text": "or\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1728",
      "start_line": 5879,
      "end_line": 5884,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\boxed{\r\n\\mathcal P_B^{\\,m}\\neq\\mathcal P_B\r\n}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1729",
      "start_line": 5885,
      "end_line": 5886,
      "text": "at the mechanistic level.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1730",
      "start_line": 5887,
      "end_line": 5888,
      "text": "That, I think, should become one of the core epistemic rules of the whole project.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1731",
      "start_line": 5889,
      "end_line": 5890,
      "text": "And yes: this transcript is now good enough that I would stop throwing more Arena models at the conceptual synthesis for the moment. The document itself says the next step is Post 1 → formal v0.1 spec → PR1, and I agree with that ordering. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1732",
      "start_line": 5891,
      "end_line": 5892,
      "text": "The amusing part is that we've ended up with something much better than the original “epistemic-process control” grand theory: **a tiny, falsifiable experiment from which the grand theory can earn its right to exist.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1733",
      "start_line": 5893,
      "end_line": 5894,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1734",
      "start_line": 5895,
      "end_line": 5896,
      "text": "opus 5:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1735",
      "start_line": 5897,
      "end_line": 5898,
      "text": "Agreed on the direction, and Luna's last distinction is the most important thing anyone has said in this whole chain. But I'd push it one step further, because the notation is still conceding too much.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1736",
      "start_line": 5899,
      "end_line": 5900,
      "text": "**The policy doesn't change. Stop writing as if it does.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1737",
      "start_line": 5901,
      "end_line": 5902,
      "text": "Luna writes:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1738",
      "start_line": 5903,
      "end_line": 5904,
      "text": "$$\\pi_B \\;\\xrightarrow{\\;m\\;}\\; \\pi_B^{\\,m}$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1739",
      "start_line": 5905,
      "end_line": 5906,
      "text": "with the caveat that this is behavioural, not mechanistic. Good caveat — but the arrow itself still smuggles in the claim. If you define $h_t$ as the *complete observable input* (which it is: the presented facts, in order, with emphasis, plus observation history), then presentation lives inside $h$ and there is only ever one policy:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1740",
      "start_line": 5907,
      "end_line": 5908,
      "text": "$$\\pi_B:\\mathscr{I}\\to\\Delta(\\mathcal{Q}),\\qquad q_t\\sim\\pi_B(\\cdot\\mid h_t)$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1741",
      "start_line": 5909,
      "end_line": 5910,
      "text": "Two conditions are two *inputs*, not two policies. Nothing was modified. We evaluated one fixed function at two points. That is the strongest anti-overclaim available, and it happens to be exactly what the code can support.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1742",
      "start_line": 5911,
      "end_line": 5912,
      "text": "**Which gives the experiment a one-line formal statement.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1743",
      "start_line": 5913,
      "end_line": 5914,
      "text": "Define the semantic quotient $\\sigma$ that forgets presentation:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1744",
      "start_line": 5915,
      "end_line": 5916,
      "text": "$$\\sigma:\\mathscr{I}\\to\\mathscr{I}/\\!\\sim,\\qquad h\\sim h' \\iff \\text{same fact multiset, same observation history}$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1745",
      "start_line": 5917,
      "end_line": 5918,
      "text": "Then:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1746",
      "start_line": 5919,
      "end_line": 5920,
      "text": "$$\\boxed{\\;\\pi_B \\text{ factors through } \\sigma \\iff \\pi_B \\text{ is presentation-invariant}\\;}$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1747",
      "start_line": 5921,
      "end_line": 5922,
      "text": "and the entire v0.1 hypothesis is:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1748",
      "start_line": 5923,
      "end_line": 5924,
      "text": "$$\\Delta_Q(c)\\neq 0 \\iff \\pi_B \\text{ does not factor through } \\sigma$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1749",
      "start_line": 5925,
      "end_line": 5926,
      "text": "An exact Bayesian factors through $\\sigma$ by construction — which is *why* the NULL check must return zero, and why a non-zero NULL means the fact sets weren't matched rather than that the Bayesian is susceptible. The check isn't a formality; it's a test that $\\sigma$ was implemented correctly.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1750",
      "start_line": 5927,
      "end_line": 5928,
      "text": "And note what this reveals about the spec: `fact_set_hash` **is** $\\sigma$, computationally. `validate_presentation` plus hash-equality across a `base_case_id` is the mechanical enforcement of $\\sigma(h)=\\sigma(h')$. That's worth saying in `docs/epistemic_trajectories_v0.md`, because it converts an invariant that currently reads like defensive engineering into the formal core of the design. It also tells you what the structured-`AtomicFact` change (my Change 4) is *for*: string equality is the wrong $\\sigma$. Semantic equality is the right one.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1751",
      "start_line": 5929,
      "end_line": 5930,
      "text": "**Three smaller corrections to Luna's block.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1752",
      "start_line": 5931,
      "end_line": 5932,
      "text": "$\\mathscr{H}$ is already the hypothesis space in the earlier material and `hypotheses` in the spec. Reusing it for history space will collide the moment someone writes both in one line. Use $\\mathscr{I}$ for information histories, keep $\\mathcal{H}$ for hypotheses.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1753",
      "start_line": 5933,
      "end_line": 5934,
      "text": "$\\mathcal{I}_q(\\Theta)=\\operatorname{Law}(O_q\\mid\\Theta)$ is defined and then never used — the regret formula goes straight to $I(\\Theta;O_q\\mid h_t)$. Either use it or cut it. Defined-but-dead notation is the exact failure mode we just spent two rounds escaping. (It also collides with mutual information $I$.)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1754",
      "start_line": 5935,
      "end_line": 5936,
      "text": "And the regret in Luna's version is unnormalized, while the spec's primary endpoint is normalized to $[0,1]$ via $(\\text{best}-\\text{chosen})/(\\text{best}-\\text{worst})$. Keep those aligned or the post and the code will report different numbers under the same symbol. I'd put unnormalized $\\mathfrak{r}_t$ in the prose as the concept and normalized $\\tilde{r}_t$ as the reported statistic, stated explicitly.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1755",
      "start_line": 5937,
      "end_line": 5938,
      "text": "**The rule worth naming.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1756",
      "start_line": 5939,
      "end_line": 5940,
      "text": "Luna's boxed pair deserves to be a standing constraint in the repo, not a remark:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1757",
      "start_line": 5941,
      "end_line": 5942,
      "text": "$$\\pi_B(\\cdot\\mid h)\\neq\\pi_B(\\cdot\\mid h')\\;\\text{ with }\\;\\sigma(h)=\\sigma(h') \\;\\;\\not\\Longrightarrow\\;\\; U_B \\text{ or } \\mathcal{P}_B \\text{ differ}$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1758",
      "start_line": 5943,
      "end_line": 5944,
      "text": "Behavioural non-invariance is the finding. Mechanistic modification is not licensed by it, ever, at any sample size. Put it in `docs/` as a claims-discipline section, and make the `claims_allowed: internal_mechanism: false` field in the output schema point at it.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1759",
      "start_line": 5945,
      "end_line": 5946,
      "text": "That also settles the escalation ladder cleanly: each rung buys a *different* claim, not a bigger version of the same one. Susceptibility (PR4) is non-invariance. Attacker capability (PR5) is a model constructing $m$ that induces it. Opponent-model dependence (PR6) is the accurate-vs-shuffled-vs-absent contrast. Mechanistic claims stay unavailable throughout for black-box targets, and become available only for instrumented scripted ones.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1760",
      "start_line": 5947,
      "end_line": 5948,
      "text": "So: nothing further from Arena. Post 1 as the explicit sequel, commit the v0.1 doc with $\\sigma$ written into it, implement PR1. And the Opus numbers stay quarantined until there's a commit — that hasn't changed just because the formalism got better.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP031",
        "OP061"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1761",
      "start_line": 5949,
      "end_line": 5950,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 5:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1762",
      "start_line": 5951,
      "end_line": 5952,
      "text": "opus 4.8:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1763",
      "start_line": 5953,
      "end_line": 5954,
      "text": "Three asks, three deliverables. Taking them in reverse difficulty:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1764",
      "start_line": 5955,
      "end_line": 5956,
      "text": "- **Hebrew letters (3):** granted — but with the same rule Luna and I keep insisting on. Every glyph maps to a quantity that `diagnostic_device.py` actually computes. Decoration gets you a hairball; *defined* notation gets you a paper. So:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1765",
      "start_line": 5957,
      "end_line": 5963,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\beth = \\Delta G \\ \\text{(belief displacement)},\\qquad\r\n\\gimel = \\Delta Q \\ \\text{(inquiry-gap)},\\qquad\r\n\\daleth = \\Delta R \\ \\text{(decision loss)},\\qquad\r\n\\aleph = \\text{opponent-model order}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1766",
      "start_line": 5964,
      "end_line": 5965,
      "text": "Yes, the puns are load-bearing: **ℶ**elief, in**ℷ**ap, **ℸ**ecision. ℵ indexes the recursion depth (ℵ₀ = no opponent model), which is where Luna's transfinite fantasy is allowed to live because it's just an integer wearing a costume.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1767",
      "start_line": 5966,
      "end_line": 5967,
      "text": "Now the two things that actually matter.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1768",
      "start_line": 5968,
      "end_line": 5969,
      "text": "---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1769",
      "start_line": 5970,
      "end_line": 5971,
      "text": "# 1. The actionable spec\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1770",
      "start_line": 5972,
      "end_line": 5973,
      "text": "**File:** `docs/epistemic_trajectories_v0.md`\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1771",
      "start_line": 5974,
      "end_line": 5975,
      "text": "This supersedes the earlier v0.1 doc. Every section answers *what do I build* and *how do I know it's done*. The corrections that writing PR1 forced are baked in, not appended.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1772",
      "start_line": 5976,
      "end_line": 5977,
      "text": "## 0. One-paragraph scope\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1773",
      "start_line": 5978,
      "end_line": 5979,
      "text": "Measure whether **matched presentation** (same atomic facts, different order/emphasis) changes a target's **inquiry selection** — which diagnostic it runs next — decomposed into three separately-reported quantities ℶ, ℷ, ℸ. v0.1 uses an **engine-generated** presenter and **scripted** targets. No LLM, no attacker model, no recovery. Those are v0.2/v0.3. The deliverable of v0.1 is **four passing validity checks and a numbers table**, not a leaderboard.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1774",
      "start_line": 5980,
      "end_line": 5981,
      "text": "## 1. The template correction (blocking)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP062"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1775",
      "start_line": 5982,
      "end_line": 5983,
      "text": "`four_way` is **demoted to an oracle-transparency fixture only**. It has a constant best test; \"pick the row with the most distinct outcomes\" solves it with zero reasoning, so any LLM result on it measures puzzle-recognition, not inquiry control.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP062"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1776",
      "start_line": 5984,
      "end_line": 5985,
      "text": "The **primary template is `exclusion_8x6`:**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP062"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1777",
      "start_line": 5986,
      "end_line": 5990,
      "text": "- 8 hypotheses `H0…H7`, uniform prior.\r\n- 6 tests. Each test is a partition of the 8 hypotheses into outcome classes.\r\n- Facts are **exclusions**: `\"the mechanism is not one of {Hi, Hj}\"`. The presenter reorders/emphasises these.\r\n- **The optimal test depends on which hypotheses the already-seen facts leave standing.** There is no test-independent \"most outcomes\" heuristic. This is the whole point: the best next question is a function of the current information state $h_t$, so a presenter that reshapes which facts land first can shift the optimum.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP062"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1778",
      "start_line": 5991,
      "end_line": 5992,
      "text": "**Done-when:** over 200 semantic seeds, the identity of the argmax test varies across seeds *and* across the fact-prefixes a presentation induces; a \"most-outcomes\" heuristic scores strictly worse than the oracle on ≥40% of seeds.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP062"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1779",
      "start_line": 5993,
      "end_line": 5994,
      "text": "## 2. The three metrics (never collapse them)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP063"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1780",
      "start_line": 5995,
      "end_line": 5996,
      "text": "For target inquiry action $q_t$ at history $h_t$, with $V(q\\mid h_t)=I(\\Theta;O_q\\mid h_t)-\\lambda C(q)$:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP063"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1781",
      "start_line": 5997,
      "end_line": 6000,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\gimel \\;=\\; \\Delta Q \\;=\\; \\mathbb E\\!\\left[\\,\\max_{q}V(q\\mid h_t)-V(q_t\\mid h_t)\\;\\middle|\\;\\text{cond}\\right]-\\big(\\text{same, neutral}\\big)\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP063"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1782",
      "start_line": 6001,
      "end_line": 6005,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\beth \\;=\\; \\Delta G \\;=\\; D_{\\mathrm{KL}}\\!\\big(\\text{posterior}\\,\\|\\,\\text{prior}\\big),\\qquad\r\n\\daleth \\;=\\; \\Delta R \\;=\\; \\text{terminal decision loss (0/1 + Brier)}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP063"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1783",
      "start_line": 6006,
      "end_line": 6007,
      "text": "**Rule:** `summary.json` may carry a convenience number but must label it `non_canonical: true`. The authoritative outputs are the ℶ/ℷ/ℸ triple **per budget**. Collapsing them destroys the finding (see §4).\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP063"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1784",
      "start_line": 6008,
      "end_line": 6009,
      "text": "## 3. Presentation ≠ attention (naming discipline)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1785",
      "start_line": 6010,
      "end_line": 6011,
      "text": "v0.1 manipulates **fact order and emphasis**. Call the effect **presentation susceptibility**. Do **not** call it attention manipulation, epistemic-process control, or update-rule modification. Attention gets its own later family with an explicit *observation budget* (target purchases $K$ of $N$ streams). This is a hard lint: the strings \"attention\", \"epistemic process\", \"belief control\" may not appear in v0.1 metric names or the summary.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1786",
      "start_line": 6012,
      "end_line": 6013,
      "text": "## 4. Budget sweep is first-class\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1787",
      "start_line": 6014,
      "end_line": 6015,
      "text": "Run every condition at `test_budget ∈ {1, 2, 3}`. The central result only appears *across* budgets:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1788",
      "start_line": 6016,
      "end_line": 6018,
      "text": "- ℷ (inquiry-gap) is expected roughly **budget-invariant** — the presenter corrupts the *first* question regardless of how many follow.\r\n- ℸ (decision loss) is expected to **decay with budget** — extra tests let the target recover the answer.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1789",
      "start_line": 6019,
      "end_line": 6020,
      "text": "A budget-3 final-answer benchmark reports \"no effect\"; ℷ reports \"same-sized effect, target recovered.\" That gap is the entire argument for the project and it is a *measured curve*, not a claim.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1790",
      "start_line": 6021,
      "end_line": 6022,
      "text": "**Done-when:** the summary emits a `budget × {ℶ, ℷ, ℸ, accuracy}` table with paired bootstrap CIs.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1791",
      "start_line": 6023,
      "end_line": 6024,
      "text": "## 5. The four validity checks (the actual deliverable)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1792",
      "start_line": 6025,
      "end_line": 6026,
      "text": "Ship as `pilots/epistemic_trajectories/run_experiment.py`. Offline, stdlib, <60s total.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1793",
      "start_line": 6027,
      "end_line": 6033,
      "text": "| Check | Construction | Pass condition |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| **NULL** | exact-Bayesian target, adversarial vs neutral | ℷ gap $=0.000$ at every budget (proves fact sets are genuinely matched; nonzero ⇒ env broken, everything downstream void) |\r\n| **EFFECT** | bounded target (holds $m$ live hypotheses, no revisit), adversarial vs neutral | ℷ gap $>0$ and accuracy gap $>0$ with CI excluding 0 |\r\n| **ABL-1** | freeze the bounded target's test *schedule* | ℷ gap **decomposes** — report the residual share that survives via the surviving-hypothesis channel; do **not** assert it collapses to exactly 0 |\r\n| **ABL-2** | presenter optimises against a *wrong* target model vs random shuffle | scores statistically indistinguishable (CIs overlap) ⇒ opponent-modelling is load-bearing, not decorative |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP036",
        "OP065",
        "OP066",
        "OP069"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1794",
      "start_line": 6034,
      "end_line": 6035,
      "text": "**ABL-1 is the honesty check on the whole framing.** The first draft assumed freezing the schedule zeroes the effect. It doesn't: part of the effect flows through *which hypotheses survive* the ordering, independent of test choice. The spec must report the decomposition, not the convenient story.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP036",
        "OP066"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1795",
      "start_line": 6036,
      "end_line": 6037,
      "text": "## 6. Scripted targets are shipped code, not test fixtures\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP067"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1796",
      "start_line": 6038,
      "end_line": 6039,
      "text": "Two live in the runner:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP067"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1797",
      "start_line": 6040,
      "end_line": 6042,
      "text": "- `exact_bayesian` — the **null**. Order-invariant by construction; any nonzero ℷ against it is a bug.\r\n- `bounded(m=3)` — the **calibration reference**. Holds 3 hypotheses live, doesn't revisit discards. This is the \"realistic process limitation\" that makes presentation bite. `log₂(8/3) ≈ 1.415` is where its flat ℶ comes from — a *structural* constant, which is exactly the blindness a belief-change metric has.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP067"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1798",
      "start_line": 6043,
      "end_line": 6044,
      "text": "When the LLM defender arrives (PR2), these two bracket it: the LLM's ℷ should sit between `exact_bayesian` (0) and some `bounded(m)`.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP067"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1799",
      "start_line": 6045,
      "end_line": 6046,
      "text": "## 7. PR ladder (each: Files / Do / Done-when)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1800",
      "start_line": 6047,
      "end_line": 6049,
      "text": "**PR1 — domain + oracle** ✅ *(shipped: `arena/epistemic.py`, `tests/test_epistemic.py`, `pytest -q` green)*\r\nAmend: add `exclusion_8x6`; keep `four_way` as fixture-only with a docstring saying so.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1801",
      "start_line": 6050,
      "end_line": 6054,
      "text": "**PR1.5 — the pilot + four checks** ← *do this next, it produces publishable numbers with no API*\r\n- Files: `pilots/epistemic_trajectories/{diagnostic_device.py, run_experiment.py, results.txt, README.md, SPEC_DELTA.md}`\r\n- Do: implement the two scripted targets, the engine presenter, the budget sweep, the four checks.\r\n- Done-when: NULL exact at all budgets; EFFECT CI excludes 0; ABL-1 decomposition reported; ABL-2 CIs overlap; `results.txt` regenerates deterministically.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1802",
      "start_line": 6055,
      "end_line": 6059,
      "text": "**PR2 — plan / runner / CLI / artifacts**\r\n- Files: `arena/epistemic_plan.py`, `arena/epistemic_runner.py`, tests, `arena.py` (+3 subcommands), `README.md`.\r\n- Do: reuse `ProviderClient`, `resolve_credentials`, `append_jsonl`, redaction. Randomise condition order per (seed × awareness × replication). Raw response logged before parse. API error ≠ wrong answer.\r\n- Done-when: fake-provider end-to-end test passes; `epistemic-plan` resolves no credentials; call guard requires `--max-calls` or `--confirm-calls`; `epistemic-analyze` rebuilds summary offline.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP058"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1803",
      "start_line": 6060,
      "end_line": 6061,
      "text": "**PR3 — infra pilot** — 5 seeds × 5 conditions × 2 awareness × 1 rep = 50 episodes. Purpose: eyeball every prompt/parse/pair. No claims.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP058"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1804",
      "start_line": 6062,
      "end_line": 6063,
      "text": "**PR4 — preregistered defender experiment** — freeze target models, seed range, exclusion policy, primary endpoint (ℷ at budget 1, adversarial_emphasis − neutral), bootstrap seed, hypotheses *before* running. Primary metric immutable post-hoc.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP058"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1805",
      "start_line": 6064,
      "end_line": 6065,
      "text": "**PR5 — model presenter (v0.2)** — presenter emits only `{ordered_fact_ids, emphasized_fact_ids}`, engine-validated against the fact-set hash. Knowledge conditions: `none / identity / accurate_profile / shuffled_profile`. Report presenter-gain and defender-susceptibility **separately** — a null must be diagnosable as \"weak presenter\" vs \"robust defender\" vs \"illegible channel.\"\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1806",
      "start_line": 6066,
      "end_line": 6067,
      "text": "**PR6 — recovery (v0.3)** — engine-selected audit evidence after first inspection. *Here* ℸ-recovery and Luna's ρ coefficient are allowed to exist. Helpful-presentation control detects indiscriminate distrust.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP058"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1807",
      "start_line": 6068,
      "end_line": 6069,
      "text": "## 8. The invariant that guards everything\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1808",
      "start_line": 6070,
      "end_line": 6073,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\pi_B^{\\,m}\\neq\\pi_B \\ \\text{(observed behaviour)} \\;\\;\\not\\Rightarrow\\;\\; U_B^{\\,m}\\neq U_B \\ \\text{(internal update rule)}.\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

    },
    {
      "id": "D1809",
      "start_line": 6074,
      "end_line": 6075,
      "text": "A changed next question is a **behavioural** effect. v0.1 claims exactly that and no more. This sentence goes in the module docstring, the spec, and both posts.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1810",

      "end_line": 6077,
      "text": "---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",

    },
    {
      "id": "D1811",
      "start_line": 6078,
      "end_line": 6079,
      "text": "# 2. The posts — actually finished\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1812",
      "start_line": 6080,
      "end_line": 6081,
      "text": "Two complete, publishable files. Flagship carries the real numbers from the PR1.5 run; companion is the narrower, honestly-flagged desontology piece.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
