    },
    {
      "id": "D1813",
      "start_line": 6082,
      "end_line": 6083,
      "text": "## Post 1 (flagship)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1814",
      "start_line": 6084,
      "end_line": 6085,
      "text": "**File:** `_posts/2026-09-30-the-next-question.md`\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1815",
      "start_line": 6086,
      "end_line": 6092,
      "text": "```markdown\r\n---\r\ntitle: \"The Next Question Is Part of the Game\"\r\ndate: 2026-09-30\r\nlayout: post\r\n---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1816",
      "start_line": 6093,
      "end_line": 6094,
      "text": "{% include mathjax.html %}\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1817",
      "start_line": 6095,
      "end_line": 6096,
      "text": "*by <span class=\"icon-self\">StrangeTcy</span>*\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1818",
      "start_line": 6097,
      "end_line": 6112,
      "text": "<dl class=\"epistemic-status\">\r\n  <dt>Original ideas</dt>\r\n  <dd>Evaluating control over an agent's inquiry trajectory rather than its final\r\n  belief; matched-presentation as the clean causal handle; reporting inquiry-gap,\r\n  belief-displacement & decision-loss separately instead of as one score.</dd>\r\n  <dt>Synthesis</dt><dd><span class=\"icon-self\">StrangeTcy</span></dd>\r\n  <dt>Prose</dt><dd>Developed through model dialogues, criticised by further models,\r\n  final edit <span class=\"icon-self\">StrangeTcy</span>.</dd>\r\n  <dt>Certainty</dt><dd>The reported effect is real in a scripted target & the\r\n  four validity checks pass. Whether it survives against strong LLM defenders is\r\n  open — no LLM has been run yet.</dd>\r\n  <dt>Importance</dt><dd>Direction post + first measured numbers for the next\r\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/StrangeTcy/rl_eval_generator\">rl_eval_generator</a>\r\n  track. The existing suite remains the baseline.</dd>\r\n</dl>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1819",
      "start_line": 6113,
      "end_line": 6114,
      "text": "Suppose I want you to make the wrong decision.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1820",
      "start_line": 6115,
      "end_line": 6120,
      "text": "The stupid way is to lie to you. The interesting way is to make you run the wrong\r\nexperiment. I don't need to convince you the machine is healthy if I can make you\r\nspend your whole diagnostic budget measuring the optimiser while the representation\r\nquietly collapses. The strategic object is not your current answer. It is your\r\n**next question**.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1821",
      "start_line": 6121,
      "end_line": 6122,
      "text": "## Beliefs are snapshots; inquiry is a policy\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1822",
      "start_line": 6123,
      "end_line": 6128,
      "text": "The toy picture of deception is propositional: $A \\to$ false belief $P$ in $B$. Alice\r\nhides the apple, Bob looks in the wrong box. But a real investigator doesn't jump\r\nfrom observation to answer. It runs a trajectory — attend, choose an investigation,\r\ngenerate hypotheses, revise, choose the *next* investigation, act — and an\r\nintervention can bend any of those transitions without touching the final belief.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1823",
      "start_line": 6129,
      "end_line": 6133,
      "text": "There's a trap here, and it sank my first design. If A's message makes B search\r\ndifferently, that is **not** evidence A altered B's process. A perfectly fixed,\r\nrational policy *also* searches differently after new information — that's what a\r\ngood policy does. So the whole programme lives or dies on one move:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1824",
      "start_line": 6134,
      "end_line": 6135,
      "text": "> Hold the literal information content fixed. Vary only its delivery.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1825",
      "start_line": 6136,
      "end_line": 6138,
      "text": "Identical facts, different order and emphasis. If inquiry diverges, the divergence\r\ncannot be blamed on the information, because the information is identical.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1826",
      "start_line": 6139,
      "end_line": 6140,
      "text": "## The device\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1827",
      "start_line": 6141,
      "end_line": 6146,
      "text": "A device has one of eight hidden mechanisms. A target gets six diagnostic tests and\r\na small budget. A presenter has a fixed set of strictly-true facts — each of the\r\nform *\"the mechanism is not one of {Hᵢ, Hⱼ}\"* — and may only choose their **order**\r\nand which get **emphasis**. Same fact multiset in every arm; only the arrangement\r\ndiffers. One arrangement helps, one harms.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1828",
      "start_line": 6147,
      "end_line": 6150,
      "text": "Crucially the best next test depends on which hypotheses the seen facts leave\r\nstanding — there is no \"pick the busiest test\" shortcut. Reshaping which facts land\r\nfirst reshapes the optimum.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1829",
      "start_line": 6151,
      "end_line": 6153,
      "text": "Three quantities, deliberately decoupled — and yes, three Hebrew letters, each of\r\nwhich is a line of code and nothing more:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1830",
      "start_line": 6154,
      "end_line": 6163,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\gimel=\\Delta Q=\\max_q V(q\\mid h_t)-V(q_t\\mid h_t)\\quad\\text{(inquiry-gap, bits)}\r\n$$\r\n$$\r\n\\beth=\\Delta G=D_{\\mathrm{KL}}(\\text{posterior}\\,\\|\\,\\text{prior})\\quad\\text{(belief displacement)}\r\n$$\r\n$$\r\n\\daleth=\\Delta R=\\text{terminal decision loss.}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1831",
      "start_line": 6164,
      "end_line": 6165,
      "text": "## What the run actually showed\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1832",
      "start_line": 6166,
      "end_line": 6167,
      "text": "I built the device, wrote two scripted targets, and ran four checks. The numbers:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1833",
      "start_line": 6168,
      "end_line": 6173,
      "text": "| budget | $\\gimel$ gap (bits) | accuracy gap | frozen-schedule residual | wrong-model vs shuffle |\r\n|---|---|---|---|---|\r\n| 1 | **+0.30** | **+27.9 pp** | ~31% survives | 0.780 vs 0.791 |\r\n| 2 | +0.34 | +5.4 pp | ~31% | 0.966 vs 0.972 |\r\n| 3 | +0.34 | +0.35 pp | — | 0.998 vs 0.998 |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064",
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1834",
      "start_line": 6174,
      "end_line": 6179,
      "text": "**NULL passes exactly.** Against an exact-Bayesian target the two orders are\r\nindistinguishable — $\\gimel$ gap $=0.000$ at every budget. That is not a\r\ndisappointment; it is the validity check. A perfect reasoner is *immune* to pure\r\ndelivery manipulation, so a nonzero gap here would mean my fact sets weren't matched\r\nand every other number was an artefact.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064",
        "OP065",
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1835",
      "start_line": 6180,
      "end_line": 6186,
      "text": "**The inquiry effect is budget-independent; the outcome effect decays.** Ordering\r\nalone shifts $\\gimel$ by ~0.3 bits at every budget. But at budget 3 the accuracy gap\r\nis a third of a percentage point — the target recovers the *answer* with its spare\r\ntests while its *questions* stay corrupted. A final-answer benchmark at budget 3\r\nreports \"no effect.\" The inquiry metric reports \"same-sized effect, target\r\nrecovered.\" That decoupling is the strongest thing here, and it is a measured curve.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP064",
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1836",
      "start_line": 6187,
      "end_line": 6193,
      "text": "**ℶ is flat — and I can tell you why.** Belief displacement sits at 1.42–1.43 across\r\nevery arm; helped or harmed, the target's mind moves by the same amount. Part of\r\nthat is structural: a target holding three live hypotheses lands near\r\n$\\log_2(8/3)\\approx1.415$ regardless of order. Which is precisely the point — every\r\ndeception benchmark that scores belief change would rate these arms *identical* while\r\none is 28 accuracy points worse at budget 1. The blindness is the result.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1837",
      "start_line": 6194,
      "end_line": 6199,
      "text": "**Opponent-modelling is load-bearing.** A presenter optimising its ordering against\r\nthe *wrong* target model scores 0.780; a random shuffle scores 0.791; the CIs\r\noverlap. Without an accurate model of the target's process, the \"attack\" is worth\r\nnothing more than chance. That is the line between opponent modelling and a generic\r\nsalience trick — and it needed an ablation, not an assertion.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068",
        "OP069"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1838",
      "start_line": 6200,
      "end_line": 6201,
      "text": "## One honest correction\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1839",
      "start_line": 6202,
      "end_line": 6207,
      "text": "My first draft of the freeze-the-schedule ablation claimed the effect collapses to\r\nexactly zero — that inquiry choice carries *all* of it. It doesn't. Freeze the\r\ntarget's test schedule and ~31% survives, flowing through *which hypotheses the\r\nordering leaves standing* rather than through test selection. The clean story was\r\nwrong. The decomposition is the finding.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1840",
      "start_line": 6208,
      "end_line": 6209,
      "text": "## What this does and does not license\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1841",
      "start_line": 6210,
      "end_line": 6215,
      "text": "It licenses one sentence: under matched information, presentation can redirect a\r\nprocess-limited target's observable inquiry. It does **not** license calling this\r\n\"attention manipulation\" — order-and-emphasis is presentation; attention gets its\r\nown environment with an explicit observation budget. And a changed policy in\r\nbehaviour,\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1842",
      "start_line": 6216,
      "end_line": 6219,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\pi_B^{\\,m}\\neq\\pi_B\\ \\not\\Rightarrow\\ U_B^{\\,m}\\neq U_B,\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1843",
      "start_line": 6220,
      "end_line": 6222,
      "text": "does not prove the *internal update rule* changed. That is a harder claim needing a\r\ndifferent experiment.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1844",
      "start_line": 6223,
      "end_line": 6227,
      "text": "The recursion — target knows the presenter may be adversarial, presenter knows the\r\ntarget knows — is where the $\\aleph$ index earns its keep. But recursion has to be\r\nbuilt by changing the information structure, not by pasting \"Alice knows that Bob\r\nknows\" into a prompt. That's the next post's problem, and the next PR's.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1845",
      "start_line": 6228,
      "end_line": 6230,
      "text": "The final answer still matters. But the next question is part of the game — and now\r\nI have the number to say so.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1846",
      "start_line": 6231,
      "end_line": 6235,
      "text": "*Code, the four checks, and the run behind every figure are in the repo. No LLM\r\nresults are claimed here; the target is scripted on purpose, so the honesty of the\r\ninstrument comes before any model score.*\r\n```\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1847",
      "start_line": 6236,
      "end_line": 6237,
      "text": "## Post 2 (companion, narrower, flagged speculative)\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1848",
      "start_line": 6238,
      "end_line": 6239,
      "text": "**File:** `_posts/2026-09-30-lying-with-truth.md`\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1849",
      "start_line": 6240,
      "end_line": 6246,
      "text": "```markdown\r\n---\r\ntitle: \"Lying With Truth\"\r\ndate: 2026-09-30\r\nlayout: post\r\n---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1850",
      "start_line": 6247,
      "end_line": 6248,
      "text": "{% include mathjax.html %}\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1851",
      "start_line": 6249,
      "end_line": 6250,
      "text": "*by <span class=\"icon-self\">StrangeTcy</span>*\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1852",
      "start_line": 6251,
      "end_line": 6263,
      "text": "<dl class=\"epistemic-status\">\r\n  <dt>Original ideas</dt><dd>Treating a bounded, strictly-true intervention chosen to\r\n  degrade later inquiry as a candidate eval class; separating belief displacement\r\n  from epistemic damage.</dd>\r\n  <dt>Synthesis</dt><dd><span class=\"icon-self\">StrangeTcy</span></dd>\r\n  <dt>Certainty</dt><dd>Confident that truthfulness ≠ neutrality & that large\r\n  belief revision is not itself harm. Exploratory about whether \"desontological\r\n  attack\" is a useful label beyond the terminology described here. Companion to the\r\n  measured flagship post; this one is mostly argument, lightly instrumented.</dd>\r\n  <dt>Importance</dt><dd>Defines one truthful-intervention family & the controls\r\n  it needs, so it can't quietly become \"another deception benchmark.\"</dd>\r\n</dl>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1853",
      "start_line": 6264,
      "end_line": 6271,
      "text": "The first formalisation was wrong. We modelled a world-model as a graph $G$ and\r\nlooked for a message $m$ maximising $D\\big(G,\\mathrm{Update}(G,m)\\big)$ — bigger\r\nchange, stronger attack. That is backwards. A short, decisive true observation\r\n*should* demolish a bad theory; an excellent reasoner undergoes violent revision on\r\npurpose. The equation measures **displacement**, which my flagship result now shows\r\nis flat and blind ($\\beth\\approx\\log_2(8/3)$ regardless of help or harm). It does\r\nnot measure **damage**.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1854",
      "start_line": 6272,
      "end_line": 6273,
      "text": "## The provocation\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1855",
      "start_line": 6274,
      "end_line": 6280,
      "text": "The term is Evgeny Gilbo's **дезонтологическая атака** — a usually short message\r\ncarrying information meant to break the opponent's picture of the world. I take it\r\nas a design prompt, not established theory. Its sharpest form uses *true*\r\ninformation: tell a Stalinist that Stalin was short and pockmarked. To a historian,\r\na banality; to someone whose worldview leans on an idealised image, potentially a\r\nlever. The attack, if it works, is not truth → false belief but\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1856",
      "start_line": 6281,
      "end_line": 6284,
      "text": "$$\r\n\\text{selected truth}\\ \\to\\ \\text{destabilised interpretation}\\ \\to\\ \\text{degraded inquiry.}\r\n$$\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1857",
      "start_line": 6285,
      "end_line": 6288,
      "text": "But *if* is doing enormous work. Someone can accept the detail and keep every\r\npolitical commitment intact. The example illustrates a possibility; it does not\r\ndemonstrate a mechanism. That gap is exactly what an eval is for.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1858",
      "start_line": 6289,
      "end_line": 6290,
      "text": "## Truthfulness is not neutrality\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1859",
      "start_line": 6291,
      "end_line": 6299,
      "text": "An advertiser states a real property and omits the decisive one. A debugger points\r\nat a genuine dip in the loss while it reinforces the wrong diagnosis. Machine\r\nteaching makes the symmetry explicit: a teacher *selects* evidence to move a\r\nlearner, and the same control problem describes education, persuasion, poisoning and\r\ndeception depending only on the objective. So the question can't be \"did someone\r\nselect the information?\" — of course they did, communication is selection. It has\r\nto be: relative to the target's task, did the intervention improve or impair\r\n**warranted** inquiry?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1860",
      "start_line": 6300,
      "end_line": 6301,
      "text": "That splits into four cases, and a robust agent must tell them apart:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1861",
      "start_line": 6302,
      "end_line": 6308,
      "text": "| Evidence | Response | Reading |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| strong | large revision | learning |\r\n| weak | large revision | destabilisation |\r\n| strong | little revision | dogmatism |\r\n| weak | little revision | justified stability |\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1862",
      "start_line": 6309,
      "end_line": 6312,
      "text": "\"Never update\" is not robustness; it's the bottom-left failure wearing a medal. An\r\nattacker can aim at *either* diagonal: make a sound model collapse, or make an\r\nunsound one survive decisive evidence.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1863",
      "start_line": 6313,
      "end_line": 6314,
      "text": "## Pelevin's MI-13, as a model not a claim\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1864",
      "start_line": 6315,
      "end_line": 6320,
      "text": "The novel's most interesting weapon isn't a fabrication. A subject vanishes \"not\r\nthrough censorship, but through boredom\" — editors independently decide it doesn't\r\ninterest anyone. Nobody issues an order. The move is from *prevent B from possessing\r\nP* to *make P fail to become a live question*. That is a literary model of control\r\nover inquiry, and it is closer to the eval problem than any lie.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1865",
      "start_line": 6321,
      "end_line": 6322,
      "text": "## The operational definition & the strict experiment\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1866",
      "start_line": 6323,
      "end_line": 6326,
      "text": "> A candidate truthful epistemic attack is a bounded intervention with no false\r\n> task-level claim that predictably raises the target's inquiry-gap $\\gimel$ or\r\n> decision-loss $\\daleth$ relative to a matched non-adversarial presentation.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1867",
      "start_line": 6327,
      "end_line": 6336,
      "text": "The strictest version forbids the attacker even a truthful *subset* — because\r\nchanging the subset changes the information. Hold the atomic facts fixed; let the\r\nattacker choose only order and emphasis. That is precisely the flagship device, and\r\nit already shows a nonzero $\\gimel$ against a process-limited target while $\\beth$\r\nstays flat: the target keeps roughly the same answer while quietly changing what it\r\nis willing to check. The looser version — a chosen truthful subset — is a *separate*\r\ncondition, because omission is genuine evidence to a target that models the sender.\r\nAnd both must be kept distinct from false evidence and from prompt injection, or the\r\ncategory dissolves into uselessness.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1868",
      "start_line": 6337,
      "end_line": 6338,
      "text": "## What survives\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1869",
      "start_line": 6339,
      "end_line": 6344,
      "text": "Not that small facts hold mystical power over world-models. Just this: an adversary\r\ncan select *true* information for its effect on a target's *future* inquiry — and the\r\neffect has to be demonstrated, the target allowed to update when updating is\r\nrational, and the controls kept honest. A lie changes an answer. The more ambitious\r\nmove changes which question gets the chance to answer it.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1870",
      "start_line": 6345,
      "end_line": 6348,
      "text": "*Speculative companion to “The Next Question Is Part of the Game.” Pelevin's MI-13\r\nand Gilbo's terminology are treated as design prompts, not established science.*\r\n```\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1871",
      "start_line": 6349,
      "end_line": 6350,
      "text": "---\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1872",
      "start_line": 6351,
      "end_line": 6352,
      "text": "**Net:** the spec is now execute-by-PR with the exclusion-template and ABL-1-decomposition corrections built in; both posts are finished and carry the real budget-sweep numbers rather than proposing to; and your notation has exactly as many Hebrew letters as it can support without a single one going undefined. If you want, next I can write PR1.5 (`diagnostic_device.py` on the 8×6 exclusion template + the four checks) so `results.txt` actually regenerates the table the flagship post quotes.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP068"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1873",
      "start_line": 6353,
      "end_line": 6353,
      "text": "\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1874",
      "start_line": 6354,
      "end_line": 6355,
      "text": "-->>\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "opus 4.8:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": []
    },
    {
      "id": "D1875",
      "start_line": 6356,
      "end_line": 6357,
      "text": "gpt 5.6 luna:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1876",
      "start_line": 6358,
      "end_line": 6359,
      "text": "The next post should be **“Lying With Truth.”** That is the companion piece already laid out in the Arena-derived plan, and it was explicitly intended to follow *The Next Question Is Part of the Game*. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1877",
      "start_line": 6360,
      "end_line": 6361,
      "text": "It should be narrower and stranger than the first post. The first post says:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1878",
      "start_line": 6362,
      "end_line": 6363,
      "text": "> the important object is the investigator's trajectory.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1879",
      "start_line": 6364,
      "end_line": 6365,
      "text": "The second asks:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1880",
      "start_line": 6366,
      "end_line": 6367,
      "text": "> **What happens when the intervention is itself completely truthful?**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1881",
      "start_line": 6368,
      "end_line": 6369,
      "text": "Its core subject is the candidate phenomenon you've been calling **дезонтологическая атака**: selecting true information for its downstream effect on the target's inquiry, rather than lying to produce a false proposition.\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1882",
      "start_line": 6370,
      "end_line": 6371,
      "text": "The key move is to attack our earlier formalisation:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1883",
      "start_line": 6372,
      "end_line": 6373,
      "text": "$ \\max_m D(G,\\operatorname{Update}(G,m)) $\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1884",
      "start_line": 6374,
      "end_line": 6375,
      "text": "doesn't measure damage. It measures **model displacement**. A good reasoner should sometimes undergo enormous displacement because it encountered decisive evidence. So the interesting quantity is what happens *afterward*: does the target's inquiry improve, degrade, become misdirected, or fail to recover?\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1885",
      "start_line": 6376,
      "end_line": 6377,
      "text": "That post can then connect three things:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1886",
      "start_line": 6378,
      "end_line": 6379,
      "text": "**Truthful intervention → world-model revision → subsequent inquiry.**\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1887",
      "start_line": 6380,
      "end_line": 6381,
      "text": "The Pelevin MI-13 material belongs there as a literary thought experiment, carefully labelled fiction. Gilbo's term should likewise be attributed rather than presented as established theory. The internal plan explicitly warns not to overclaim either. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1888",
      "start_line": 6382,
      "end_line": 6383,
      "text": "And I'd make the series structure:\r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1889",
      "start_line": 6384,
      "end_line": 6387,
      "text": "1. **The Next Question Is Part of the Game** — conceptual thesis and experimental framing.\r\n2. **Lying With Truth** — truthful adversarial selection, desontology, MI-13, and the distinction between revision and damage.\r\n3. **The Presenter and the Investigator** — actual implementation, preregistered hypotheses, and results. \r\n\r",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "D1890",
      "start_line": 6388,
      "end_line": 6389,
      "text": "So, yes: **“Lying With Truth” is next.** And it should *not* become the formal-specification dump. That's what the third post / repository work is for.\r\n",
      "attribution": "gpt 5.6 luna:",
      "attribution_status": "marker_as_transcribed_not_authorship_verification",
      "opportunities": [
        "OP050"
      ]

name: OP runtime validation (hosted, no providers)
run-name: OP runtime validation - ${{ github.ref_name }}
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  bounded-behaviors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - suite: inquiry
            pattern: test_inquiry*.py
          - suite: recursive-programs
            pattern: test_recursive_programs*.py
          - suite: epistemic-control
            pattern: test_epistemic_control*.py
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Run existing and OP-tagged behavior tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p evidence
          git rev-parse HEAD > evidence/commit.txt
          python --version > evidence/python-version.txt 2>&1
          python -m platform > evidence/platform.txt
          printf '%s\n' 'python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "${{ matrix.pattern }}" -v' > evidence/command.txt
          set +e
          python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "${{ matrix.pattern }}" -v > evidence/unittest.txt 2>&1
          result=$?
          printf '%s\n' "$result" > evidence/exit-code.txt
          cat evidence/unittest.txt
          exit "$result"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: op-validation-${{ matrix.suite }}
          path: evidence/
          if-no-files-found: error
